title: From Structure to Semantics: Hypergraph-Based AR Assembly Guidance with LLM-Mediated Narration
venue: IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics
abstract: Effective Augmented Reality (AR) guidance for complex assembly faces a dual challenge: the inability of conventional liaison graphs to represent procedural logic, and the cognitive burden imposed by visual instructions. We argue that the solution requires a more expressive structure to overcome these representational deficits and a narration approach to mediate instruction complexity. Our method first employs an assembly hypergraph to capture the task's hierarchical information, from which an A* search algorithm generates an optimal assembly path. Then a Large Language Model (LLM)-mediated narration workflow is designed to address the ergonomic deficiencies of the machine-centric path. It employs an optimizer to improve fluency, followed by a narrator that crafts the steps into an intuitive instruction narration. A within-subjects user study (N = 24) revealed a progressive enhancement from our method's components. The transition from a liaison-graph baseline to the hypergraph alone improved objective outcomes by reducing task time and errors and improving subjective ratings (SUS, NASA-TLX, TAM, and ARI). Subsequently, augmenting the LLM-mediated narration maintained these gains while lowering cognitive load and elevating user experience and usability. Our findings indicate the value of our AR assembly design and discuss the opportunities of using LLM as a mediation layer for better user interaction. © 1995-2012 IEEE.

title: From the Perspective of Artificial Intelligence: Design and Application of Song Brocade Patterns Based on the Theory of Qualia
venue: Proceedings of the 2nd International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Interaction Design
abstract: This study aims to precisely classify user demands using generative artificial intelligence tools, addressing the issue of insufficient quantification of users' emotional needs in cultural and creative product design related to Song Brocade patterns. It proposes an innovative design strategy based on the Theory of Qualia and generative AI technology to enhance the cultural identity and market competitiveness of such products. A qualia model is constructed around product imagery, behavioral preference, and emotional identity as its three core dimensions. The Kano model and K-means clustering analysis are employed to classify the preferences of 129 users. The Song Brocade patterns are generated and trained using the LoRA model to achieve visual optimization, with the design outcomes subsequently validated through user evaluation. According to the K-means clustering analysis of user classifications, the “Cultured-Elegant” group prefers historical connotations, while the “Functional-Practical” group focuses on convenience. Based on these findings, culturally adaptive patterns are generated. This strategy provides significant insights for the refined development and industrial advancement of intangible cultural heritage cultural and creative products.

title: From Visit to Reflection: A Narrative Interaction Design Approach for Continuity in Virtual Museum Experiences with LLMs
venue: International Journal of Human-Computer Interaction
abstract: Virtual museums have become an important form of cultural experience, yet narrative support often remains limited to individual exhibits or isolated phases of a visit. We define this as a problem of narrative continuity and address it through narrative interaction design. A multi-stakeholder formative study identified three design considerations: spatial structuring, relational interpretation, and reflective feedback. We instantiated these in NarraTour, a virtual museum prototype using bounded large language model-supported functions grounded in curated museum data and recorded interaction traces. A within-subject study (N = 24) across four configurations showed that spatial support establishes narrative progression, relational support is most effective when aligned with visitors’ progression, and reflective support extends continuity beyond exploration by enabling retrospective sense-making. We contribute a narrative interaction design approach for sustaining continuity across virtual museum experiences and empirical insights into when and how different forms of narrative support should be introduced. © 2026 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.

title: Future Smart Devices in Future Digital Environments
venue: European Conference on Information Warfare and Security, ECCWS
abstract: Our modern smart cities and societies are rapidly changing in all aspects. These entities can be described as digital, multidimensional hybrid entities, where everything is interconnected and where different technologies are used to acquire, transmit, exchange, process, use, and store information. We need to look at these multidimensional information and communication system entities in a new way. The information and data models we use, and their functionalities, require communication systems that consist of air-space-land-sea communication networks (ASGM), in which the different components work seamlessly together. These digital, multidimensional hybrid systems include several parts and functions, such as various digital platforms and their services; a range of technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), and virtual reality (VR) solutions; blockchains; digital twins; quantum technologies (communication, cryptography, and computing); metaverse environments; and various data center functions. These environments also use the Large Language Model (LLM). Our new smart devices must be developed to adapt and operate in these environments, using the services they provide, and they must function regardless of time and place across all usage contexts, including extraterrestrial networks. Data center capabilities, MECs, and edge systems are also rapidly evolving due to emerging communication requirements. Quantum computing, cryptography, and communication, alongside ML, are becoming available, and their integration must be explored, as they introduce additional challenges for device design and functionality. We must ensure sufficiently low transmission and synchronization latencies so that physical and virtual environments can interact seamlessly without failures. In this article, we examine smart devices designed for future communication environments. These devices will utilize artificial intelligence, machine learning, and virtual reality to support the services of future smart societies across operational domains, including those beyond Earth. We also analyze cybersecurity threats to end-to-end services in different use cases and explore device-level functional enhancements. © 2026 Curran Associates Inc.. All rights reserved.

title: G-MAO: Gaze-Grounded Multi-Agent Orchestration for XR Document Understanding
venue: International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks, ICUFN
abstract: Extended Reality (XR) environments are increas-ingly used for productivity tasks involving large language models (LLMs), such as document reading and analysis in multi-window workspaces. However, existing XR-based LLM systems face two major challenges: selecting relevant context from multiple con-current views and coordinating reasoning across multiple agents without overwhelming users. While prior gaze-aware approaches mainly focus on context selection, most systems still rely on single-agent architectures that struggle with document-level reasoning and temporal continuity. To address these limitations, we propose a gaze-grounded multi-agent orchestration framework for XR document understanding. The framework interprets users' gaze behaviors as probabilistic signals of cognitive states, including local comprehension, global exploration, and temporal connec-tion. Based on these signals, the system dynamically activates specialized reasoning agents, including a Gaze Agent, Global Agent, and Memory Agent. A synthesis module integrates outputs from multiple agents into unified responses to reduce information overload and role ambiguity. We present the system architecture and discuss its potential for improving interaction efficiency and adaptive reasoning support in XR document understanding environments. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Gamified Learning Using Augmented Reality and LLM-Powered Chatbots for Teaching Kepler’s Laws
venue: 2026 IEEE Global Engineering Education Conference (EDUCON)
abstract: This study evaluated the impact of a gamified intervention integrating augmented reality (AR) and large language model (LLM)-powered chatbots on teaching Kepler's laws to first-year engineering students. A pretest-posttest design was implemented with 180 participants who took part in a 90-minute collaborative activity titled Discovering Planetary Motion. Organized into physical stations corresponding to each law, students used a custom AR application to visualize orbital mechanics and interacted with AI "space travelers"(chatbots trained using Ollama LLM) to solve guided challenges. Learning gains were assessed through parallel pre-and post-activity surveys featuring Likert-scale and multiple-choice questions. Results showed significant improvements in conceptual understanding: the proportion of students strongly agreeing that planetary motion is predictable increased by 11.4%, and strong disagreement was entirely eliminated. Comprehension of Kepler's second law (that planetary speed is greatest at perihelion) rose sharply from 78.4% to 97.7%. Understanding of the third law showed a measured increase from 87.5% to 92%, a 4.5% gain, while comprehension of Kepler's first law remained relatively stable, with a slight decrease from 96% to 94.9% after the activity. Students responded very positively to the intervention, with 88.0% indicating that AR increased their interest in learning and 94.9% reporting that the chatbots promoted reflective thinking. These findings demonstrate that combining gamified AR with conversational AI can markedly enhance the understanding of complex scientific concepts, providing an engaging and effective model for implementing active, immersive learning in STEM education. © 2026 IEEE.

title: GAVIA-X: Interactive Diffusion Inpainting for Generative AI-Driven VR/XR Content
venue: Proceedings - 2026 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and eXtended and Virtual Reality, AIxVR 2026
abstract: In this paper, we introduce GAVIA-X, an extension of the GAVIA framework that transforms a methodology for Generative AI (GenAI) content extension into an interactive visualization and correction mechanism for the generation of 3D environments from Large Language Model (LLM) prompts for Virtual and Mixed Realities (VR/XR). The main contribution is a novel system that overcomes the challenges of Diffusion models to produce smooth and consistent 360° panoramic cubemaps by involving a Gemma-based LLM to automatically generate contextual prompts and an interactive, VR/XR-ready inpainting mechanism through an A-Frame plug-in. Based on an A-Frame plugin, the system provides a VR/XR experience in which users can 'paint' masks on the 3D cubemap face in order to fix GenAI artifacts, or customize scenes, and employs morphological operators (dilation and closing) to smooth the masks and produce seamless transitions for a better VR/XR. The most promising use cases are the generation of customized datasets for World Models (WM) training and synthetic backgrounds, facilitating the training with human supervision. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Gaze-informed vlm agents with symbolic knowledge for vr art experiences
venue: Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence and Applications
abstract: Recent advances in Virtual Reality, conversational AI, and multimodal interaction have opened new opportunities for enhancing visitor engagement in cultural heritage settings. This paper investigates a conversational agent for virtual art exploration that integrates real-time gaze tracking, vision-language models (VLMs), and structured semantic knowledge to support adaptive dialogue in a virtual art exhibition. Gaze coordinates serve as an implicit signal of user attention, guiding VLM-based visual interpretation and enabling context-aware responses grounded in a domain-specific knowledge graph. We report preliminary findings across three evaluation stages: (1) an initial assessment of VLM performance on gaze-driven visual interpretation with and without semantic context; (2) a qualitative comparison of a gaze-informed agent with a manually annotated Areas of Interest (AOI) baseline; and (3) a between-subjects user study with 27 participants examining enjoyment, engagement, personalization, collaboration, and gaze awareness. Results suggest that gaze-driven AOI inference is a viable alternative to manually predefined AOIs: it often produces more fine-grained, gaze-contingent interpretations while maintaining comparable user experience to the baseline condition. These findings motivate further investigation into semantically grounded, gaze-responsive conversational agents as a potential approach to personalized interaction in immersive cultural environments. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Gbp-llm: gaze behavior prediction in 6DoF VR via large language models
venue: Multimedia Systems
abstract: Accurately predicting user gaze behavior is critical for intelligent and responsive interaction in six-degrees-of-freedom (6DoF) virtual reality (VR), enabling latency-sensitive functions such as attention-aware interaction and proactive rendering. In such scenarios, gaze behavior is jointly determined by head translation, head rotation, and eye gaze direction, and is further modulated by scene-dependent visual saliency as well as user and scene context. Existing methods often model only a subset of these factors and fuse multimodal cues via simple concatenation or static projection, which fails to enforce cross-modal geometric consistency and semantic alignment, resulting in limited generalization under constrained training data. We propose GBP-LLM, a foundation-model-driven framework that leverages a frozen large language model (LLM) as a unified sequence backbone for geometric-semantic fusion. Specifically, a Triangle Encoder models the geometric relationship between head pose and eye gaze, producing geometry-aware representations that provide the basis for aligning saliency cues with head-eye signals in a shared spatial space. Built upon this geometric basis, a structured prompting module extracts saliency information together with system context to guide multimodal reasoning. Experiments on our self-collected dataset and the public FixationNet-dataset demonstrate that GBP-LLM consistently outperforms conventional deep learning baselines on 6DoF gaze behavior prediction, and ablation studies verify the contribution of geometric encoding and each prompt component. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.

title: GeMR : Multi-modal Interactive 3D Scene Composition In XR
venue: Proceedings of ICVGIP 2025 - 16th Indian Conference on Computer Vision, Graphics and Image Processing
abstract: This paper introduces a novel mixed-reality (MR) 3D authoring platform designed to enable real-time, interactive composition of 3D scenes in augmented and mixed reality environments. The platform proposed and integrates two key innovations: a three-tier 3D asset generation workflow and a 3D sketch-to-shape retrieval algorithm. The three-tier architecture addresses the challenge of time-consuming 3D asset creation by allowing users to engage with the generation process at intermediate stages, enabling rapid validation and refinement of user inputs. This approach not only enhances interactivity but also accelerates the realization of user imagined assets. Complementing this is our 3D sketch-to-shape retrieval system, which leverages an intuitive, robust sketching module to query a library of generated or artist-created 3D assets. This mechanism facilitates precise retrieval of objects matching both the category and rough shape of a user drawn 3D sketch of the assets. The platform supports multi-modal, intuitive user inputs such as speech, text, and freehand 3D sketches, making it accessible to both novice and expert users for creating, retrieving, modifying, and composing 3D assets and textures. By combining generative models with intuitive interaction, the platform serves as a flexible testbed for 3D asset development and a tool to democratize 3D scene authoring. We show effectiveness of GeMR on various use-cases, including scenario composition for human-robot collaboration. We conducted a user study to evaluate whether our system effectively democratizes the 3D scene composition. We compared the performance of 3D modeling experts and novice users on a standardized scene creation task. Both novice and expert users reported equally good usability ratings and low perceived workload. Our findings highlight that an integration of generative models and multimodal intuitive inputs represents a significant leap in making the 3D scene authoring more accessible. © 2025 Copyright held by the owner/author(s).

title: GEN-AI + VR: Toward an Experiential Visual Communication Framework in Interior Architecture
venue: AI and the Transformation of Visual Culture, Art, and Design
abstract: This chapter examines the intersection of generative artificial intelligence and immersive virtual reality as a transformative shift in the communicative structure of architectural representation. It aims to reconceptualize representation not as a linear process ofvisual production but as a multilayeredsystem ofmediation through which spatial meaning is progressively constructed. The chapter outlines how linguistic input, algorithmic interpretation, visual synthesis, volumetric modeling, and immersive experience operate as interconnected stages within a unified framework. Through this perspective, representation is positioned as a dynamic and iterative process shaped by feedback loops between human intention and computational systems. The proposed AI–IVR mediated framework highlights how design knowledge is generated, evaluated, and reformulated across semantic, visual, geometric, and experiential domains, offering a conceptual model for understanding contemporary interior architectural practice. title: GenAI avatars in VR: Role of presence, health, and technological factors
venue: Computers and Education: X Reality
abstract: In higher education, VR environments increasingly include Generative AI (GenAI) avatars, but it is unclear how user expectations, presence, and health relate to continued engagement. We examined these relationships in an AI literacy activity ( N = 30) in which students interacted with two avatars of GPT (one RAG, one non-RAG) using the Educational VR platform Classlet. Using surveys, system logs, and coded dialogues, we observed that participants reporting higher technological expectations were less likely to proceed to the second avatar when interaction issues occurred. In regression models, presence was more closely associated with perceived functionality and self-reported health than with visual realism in this sample ( R 2 = 0.538 for presence; R 2 = 0.782 for intent). Dialogue coding showed a modest difference in contextual relevance. Taken together, the results suggest that expectation management and interaction fluency may be important for continuation decisions, and that usability and comfort may support presence alongside immersion. We discuss implications for VR adoption (expectancy violations), presence as tied to operational factors, and the role of adaptive dialogue, noting that these patterns warrant confirmation in larger, diverse samples. © 2026 The Authors.

title: GenARate Together: Investigating Collaborative Image Generation Through Tangible Interaction
venue: AHs 2026 - Augmented Humans 2026
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) allows image creation through graph-based tools, yet these systems become complex quickly. We implemented a tangible user interface (TUI) and a tablet system to simplify image generation. We investigated how social context influences the user experience and sense of agency regarding the interaction modality. In a within-subject lab study with 24 participants, the tangible interface showed a significantly increased hedonic quality, while the tablet scored higher on pragmatic quality. Participants described the tangible interface as promoting collaboration, parallel work, and playful engagement, while valuing the tablet for efficiency. They also emphasized that supporting user agency required balancing the clarity of tangible interaction with the flexibility of text-based input methods. Finally, participants highlighted the potential of such systems to promote AI literacy for children and novices, while raising ethical concerns about misuse and the lack of recognition of original content in GenAI. © 2026 Copyright held by the owner/author(s).

title: GenAssist: Interactive Prompt-Driven XR Program Generation
venue: Proceedings - 2026 IEEE Conference on Virtual Reality and 3D User Interfaces, VR 2026
abstract: This paper introduces GenAssist, a system for generating interactive Extended Reality (XR) programs from natural language prompts. Given plain text descriptions of desired programs, our system uses Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to retrieve related documentation and example code, which is then used to prompt Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate and execute hot-pluggable XR programs in real time. To ensure that the programs are written correctly to the user's specifications, we add a closed-loop feedback mechanism using virtual cameras in the scene that iteratively refines the system's output, mimicking the development cycle of human developers that compile and then interactively test programs. GenAssist generates scripts that can not only place multiple primitives and 3D models in various locations in a virtual scene, but it can also animate and enable user interactions with those objects. We show that across a benchmark of 50 diverse XR program prompts, our system achieves high output accuracy and program generation quality. Furthermore, we conduct a user study with 18 participants that demonstrates GenAssist's effectiveness and usability (NASA TLX = 36.6) for XR program generation. We compare GenAssist to prior systems and show that it is significantly faster (<10 seconds per run) and requires fewer LLM calls. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Gender Differences in AI-Powered Virtual Museum Guides: Learning Outcomes and Interaction Patterns in Immersive VR
venue: TechTrends
abstract: Generative AI and virtual reality are transforming educational and cultural experiences by enabling interactive, personalized, and immersive environments. This study employed a mixed-method sequential explanatory design to investigate gender-specific differences in user engagement, interaction patterns, and learning outcomes within AI-powered virtual museum environments. Sixty university students (30 males and 30 females) participated, engaging with AI-driven virtual assistants through VR headsets. Quantitative analyses using independent t-tests revealed that while both genders achieved significant knowledge gains, females demonstrated higher task-focused engagement and more fact- and clarification-oriented interactions, whereas males favored exploratory and entertainment-oriented queries. Qualitative thematic analysis further highlighted gender-specific preferences in system design and AI communication styles. The findings underscore the importance of designing adaptive AI systems that account for diverse interaction styles and learning needs. Recommendations include integrating gamification, enhancing AI responsiveness, and tailoring communication approaches to foster inclusive and equitable educational experiences. © Association for Educational Communications & Technology 2026.

The findings underscore the importance of designing adaptive AI systems that account for diverse interaction styles and learning needs. Recommendations include integrating gamification, enhancing AI responsiveness, and tailoring communication approaches to foster inclusive and equitable educational experiences. © Association for Educational Communications & Technology 2026.

title: Generating Audiovisual Synergy Fluid Animation for Highly Immersive VR Experience
venue: IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics
abstract: Generative content is increasingly applied in VR to provide immersive experiences, yet maintaining high generation quality remains challenging for audiovisual effects. Particularly in dynamic fluid phenomena, achieving realism and presence requires adherence to physical laws. To accomplish this objective, this work proposes an audiovisual synergy fluid animation generation framework, which enhances immersion by improving motion texture fidelity and audiovisual consistency. It comprises Detail-Enhanced Texture generator (DET) and Physics-Guided Audio generator (PGA). DET integrates Global-Local Physics guidance (GLP) and Temporal Texture Modeling (TTM) to produce video textures, explicitly optimizing dynamic details by leveraging local motion cues and assigned cumulative differences. PGA incorporates Visual Semantic Augmenter (VSA) and Rhythm Semantic Adapter (RSA) to synchronize audio by fusing static visual semantics with dynamic motion semantics to improve temporal coherence. By integrating DET and PGA, this framework strengthens audiovisual immersion in VR natural dynamic scenes from both visual and auditory perspectives. Quantitative and qualitative evaluations demonstrate that our approach surpasses most existing methods in terms of texture realism and audiovisual synchronization, offering new insights for advancing immersive experiences in dynamic VR phenomena. © 1995-2012 IEEE.

title: Generative AI and Augmented Reality for Personalized Biophilic Design in Senior Living Environments
venue: Construction Research Congress 2026: Advanced Technologies, Artificial Intelligence, and Data Analytics in Construction - Selected papers from Construction Research Congress 2026
abstract: Biophilic design, which integrates natural elements into built environments, has been shown to support cognitive, affective, and physical well-being in older adults. However, physical biophilic interventions are costly, space-intensive, and often difficult to retrofit in senior living facilities. This paper presents a generative AI-supported augmented reality (AR) approach for biophilic design, enabling seniors to experience personalized and scalable biophilic environments. We developed a four-stage prompting pipeline to generate diverse 3D biophilic assets, which were integrated into a Unity-based AR application deployable on mobile and tablet devices. A preliminary pilot experiment with two participants explored cognitive and affective responses using Stroop and PANAS measures, alongside exit surveys capturing user perceptions. Results indicated individual variability in cognitive responses, stable affective states across conditions, and generally positive evaluations of the biophilic AR environment. These findings provide proof-of-concept evidence for the feasibility and experiential potential of generative AI-supported biophilic AR in senior living contexts. Future work will involve larger cohorts, validated usability measures, and comparative evaluation with physical biophilic environments. © 2026 ASCE.

title: Generative AI + AR: a novel embodied conversational agent in an interactive learning environment
venue: Interactive Learning Environments
abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (Generative AI) and Augmented Reality (AR) have garnered increasing attention from researchers for their application in the field of education. Investigating how to integrate Generative AI in a visual way into real classrooms is one of the directions for the deep integration of information technology and science education in the future. This study designed and developed an AR-based embodied conversational agent (ECA) Virtual Scientist and explored its impact on students’ learning outcomes and experience. A total of 62 primary school students participated in a four-week experiment, in which the quantitative and qualitative data were collected to be analyzed through covariance analysis and thematic analysis. It is found that the intervention of the AR-based embodied conversational agent significantly enhanced students’ critical thinking, inquisitiveness and learning motivation. Moreover, students positively evaluated the technology. This study provides experience and strategies for the development and practical classroom application of Generative AI-based AR learning environment, offering practical guidance for the implementation of human–computer teaching. © 2025 Informa UK Limited, trading as Taylor & Francis Group.

title: Generative AI as a Learning Partner: Structural Insights from a VR–GPT Educational Platform
venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science
abstract: Virtual reality (VR) enhanced by Generative AI (GenAI) avatars offers opportunities for adaptive and engaging educational experiences. While prior studies emphasize the roles of performance expectancy (PE) and technological efficacy (TE) in learner engagement, few examined how AI scaffolding influences metacognition (META), agency, and motivational beliefs in VR. This study applied structural equation modeling (SEM) to investigate these dynamics in two experimental groups in low-immersive VR (desktops). The model demonstrated acceptable fit (CFI = 0.912, TLI = 0.887) and R2 values were highest for intention and technological efficacy (both > 0.70), with metacognition at 0.491. PE predicted both intention to continue using the system and TE, while GPT interaction increased META. However, META negatively predicted PE, suggesting a trade-off between reflection and system use. These results highlight the importance of designing AI scaffolding that supports metacognitive processes without undermining motivation. Integrating AI within VR environments can better align with learner expectations and improve both engagement and learning outcomes. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.

title: Generative AI-Assisted Visualization Prototyping for Cultural Heritage: A Computational Framework from 2D Planes to 3D Immersive Scenes
venue: Buildings
abstract: Immersive visualization can support interpretation of architectural heritage in historical paintings, yet translating 2D pictorial evidence into navigable 3D scenes remains challenging. Conventional workflows rely on physical survey data, while direct generative AI (GenAI) may produce structural hallucinations and lack historical constraints. This study proposes a human-in-the-loop GenAI-assisted framework for producing immersive 3D visualization prototypes rather than historically verified reconstructions. It integrates multi-view image generation, knowledge-informed review, single-image-to-3D generation, topology inspection, and perceptual calibration. Four fragments from the Northern Song Dynasty painting Along the River During the Qingming Festival were examined as a single-case proof of concept. Across three tested model pairs, raw AI assets were generated in approximately 3–4 min and were suitable for distant-background use; close-up visualization required 1–2 h of refinement, while basic structural editability required 4–5 h of post-processing, reducing the initial time advantage. A mixed-methods study with nine domain experts and 30 non-expert participants used the UES-SF, an adapted VisAWI, and semi-structured interviews analyzed through inductive thematic analysis. All eight subscale scores exceeded their neutral midpoints after Bonferroni correction (all adjusted (Formula presented.)), indicating favorable perceptions of the guided experience. Interviews suggested potential for spatial exploration, museum interpretation, and education. However, geometric discontinuities, detail loss, color deviation, and historical-semantic errors remained, requiring expert review and manual correction. Transferability beyond this artwork and architectural tradition remains untested. © 2026 by the authors.

title: Generative AI-Driven Metaverse: The Promises and Challenges of AI-Generated Content
venue: IEEE Open Journal of the Computer Society
abstract: Recent advancements in Artificial Intelligence (AI) and immersive technologies, such as Extended Reality (XR), coupled with complementary innovations like 5G/6G wireless communications, are paving the way for fully realized AI-XR metaverses. AI will play a pivotal role in this transformation, enabling the seamless convergence of virtual and physical worlds. Among the various AI applications, Generative AI (GenAI) stands out for creating rich, dynamic, and interactive virtual environments—essential elements for sustained metaverse growth and user engagement. To facilitate a deeper understanding of how GenAI will be integrated and utilized within the metaverse, we provide a comprehensive overview of GenAI and Artificial Intelligence-Generated Content (AIGC). Specifically, we examine the potential influence of GenAI's on future metaverses, exploring both the opportunities it offers and the major challenges associated with its deployment. Additionally, we investigate the robustness of AIGC detection techniques against adversarial attacks, highlighting less-explored risks posed by adversarial examples. Finally, we highlight various open research issues related to GenAI, AIGC, the metaverse, and responsible innovation that merit further exploration. © 2020 IEEE.

title: Generative AI-Driven Virtual Reality for Health Consultation Training in School Nursing
venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science
abstract: The rapid evolution of immersive technology has significantly expanded the potential for virtual reality to facilitate clinical communication training within medical and nursing education. To address the limitations of traditional role-playing, which often struggles to replicate the complex and resistant behaviors of pediatric patients, this study develops a generative-AI-driven VR health consultation training system. The system incorporates a trust-based interaction control mechanism, utilizing large language models to evaluate verbal strategies in real-time and dynamically adjust the virtual child’s behavioral responses and trust levels. A multimodal learning analytics approach was employed to capture and analyze the spatial behaviors, physiological signals, and subjective evaluations of four pre-service school nurses across scenarios of varying children’s personalities. Experimental results demonstrate that the system effectively simulates distinct scenarios, where the integration of these multimodal datasets reveals specific behavioral and physiological patterns that distinguish between effective and ineffective communication trajectories. This research validates the complementary value of such data in assessing complex consultation skills and provides an empirical foundation for the development of personalized, adaptive intelligent training platforms. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.

title: Generative AI Features and Limitations in Support of Inclusive XR Immersive Learning Environments for Aging and Creative Community Applications
venue: KSII Transactions on Internet and Information Systems
abstract: This survey examines how Generative AI (GenAI) influences the development of inclusive immersive learning environments built on Extended Reality (XR). While GenAI enhances XR through multimodal content generation, adaptive feedback, and real-time scene construction, its probabilistic nature introduces structural limitations—including reasoning inconsistency, contextual drift, multimodal desynchronization, strategic adaptation gaps, and ethical opacity—that can undermine reliability in multisensory, latency-sensitive contexts. Drawing on global XR market trends, policy frameworks, and cross-domain case studies in education, healthcare, creative practice, and civic participation, the survey analyzes how these limitations manifest in practice. It proposes inclusive design principles and a conceptual improvement framework integrating multimodal alignment learning, domain-specific fine-tuning, reinforcement-based adaptation, explainable generative interfaces, and hybrid edge–cloud architectures, while acknowledging associated computational trade-offs. To support empirical validation, the paper introduces a multidimensional evaluation model encompassing cross-modal fidelity, semantic integrity, cognitive stability, contextual continuity, and adaptive transparency. An illustrative application scenario and a minimal experimental protocol demonstrate how these dimensions may be operationalized. Overall, the survey provides an analytical and evaluative foundation for developing reliable and inclusive GenAI-enhanced XR learning systems for aging populations and creative communities. © 2026 KSII.

title: Generative AI for Immersive Environment Design: A Systematic Review of Deep Learning in Virtual World Creation
venue: Proceedings of the 2nd International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Interaction Design
abstract: The rapid evolution of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) is reshaping workflows for virtual world construction, complementing manual geometric modeling with latent-space-driven synthesis. This systematic review synthesizes empirical evidence regarding the effectiveness of Deep Learning (DL) architectures, specifically Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), Diffusion Models, and Neural Radiance Fields (NeRFs), in facilitating immersive environment design and its subsequent impact on user cognition. Following the PRISMA protocol, 50 peer-reviewed empirical studies published between 2015 and 2025 were analyzed to evaluate the synergy between AI-driven environmental fidelity and human information processing. The findings, grounded in Dual-Coding Theory and Cognitive Load Theory, reveal a distinct divergence in system component efficacy: while DL-optimized “multimedia features” such as realistic rendering and intelligent soundscapes significantly enhance spatial presence and narrative comprehension, non-congruent “interactive functions” and excessive gamification frequently precipitate cognitive overload. The results indicate that AI-mediated environments bolster emergent spatial literacy and vocabulary acquisition primarily when “temporal and spatial contiguity” is maintained between generative assets and core task content. However, the “novelty effect” often masks a conflict between algorithmic complexity and the user's limited cognitive capacity, leading to fragmented retention in highly interactive but poorly structured environments. This review concludes by offering a theoretical framework for “narrative-first” design, providing critical guidelines for developers and educators to ensure that technological scaffolding enhances, rather than hampers, deep cognitive engagement in the era of Generative AI.

title: Generative-AI for XR Content Transmission in the Metaverse: Potential Approaches, Challenges, and a Generation-Driven Transmission Framework
venue: IEEE Network
abstract: How to efficiently transmit large volumes of Extended Reality (XR) content through current networks has been a major bottleneck in realizing the Metaverse. The recently emerging Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) has already revolutionized various technological fields and provides promising solutions to this challenge. In this article, we first demonstrate current networks’ bottlenecks for supporting XR content transmission in the Metaverse. Then, we explore the potential approaches and challenges of utilizing GAI to overcome these bottlenecks. To address these challenges, we propose a GAI-based XR content transmission framework which leverages a cloud-edge collaboration architecture. The cloud servers are responsible for storing and rendering the original XR content, while edge servers utilize GAI models to generate essential parts of XR content (e.g., subsequent frames, selected objects, etc.) when network resources are insufficient to transmit them. A Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL)-based decision module is proposed to solve the decision-making problems. Our case study demonstrates that the proposed GAI-based transmission framework achieves a 2.8-fold increase in normal frame ratio (percentage of frames that meet the quality and latency requirements for XR content transmission) over baseline approaches, underscoring the potential of GAI models to facilitate XR content transmission in the Metaverse. © 1986-2012 IEEE.

title: Generative AI in Game Development: A Bibliometric Study with an Auditable Computing Workflow
venue: Proceedings of the 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Interaction Design
abstract: This paper presents a bibliometric mapping of generative AI in game development from 2017 to 2025, covering 1,103 publications retrieved under a dual-axis query of model families (e.g., GANs, diffusion models, LLMs) and development components (e.g., PCG, game assets, NPCs, engines). Using CiteSpace and VOSviewer, we analyze co-occurrence, co-citation, and cluster structures to reveal the field's evolution from algorithm-driven (genetic/evolutionary) to data-driven (deep learning, GAN) and experience-driven (LLM-NPCs, dynamic difficulty, serious games) trajectories. To meet EI/Scopus expectations for computer-application rigor and reproducibility, we document the end-to-end computing workflow (query to de-duplication to text normalization to co-occurrence/cluster construction), fix random seeds, and report lightweight engineering metrics (step-wise runtime and peak memory). We also list software versions and key parameters (time slicing, Pathfinder pruning, LLR labeling; modularity Q and silhouette S) to make figures and tables auditable. The study consolidates trends, pinpoints core venues and authors, and offers a concise, reusable recipe for bibliometric mining in AI-for-games

title: Generative AI, virtual reality simulation and communication entrustment in competency-based medical education
venue: Curriculum Journal
abstract: Competency-based medical education (CBME) requires learners to demonstrate communication as observable professional practice rather than theoretical knowledge. Immersive virtual reality (VR) simulation provides authentic opportunities to rehearse challenging clinical conversations, while generative artificial intelligence (AI) offers new possibilities for communication training. This correspondence argues that AI should function as a bounded reflective scaffold rather than as a substitute for live communicative performance. AI can support preparation and post-simulation reflection by helping learners explore alternative responses, clarify reasoning and strengthen reflective practice. However, during simulated or assessed encounters, communication should remain entirely learner-enacted to preserve the validity of entrustment decisions. Positioning AI outside the live interaction maintains professional agency, ensures assessment is based on observable human performance and protects the integrity of competency-based progression. Establishing clear curricular boundaries allows educators to integrate AI into communication training while preserving the educational purposes of CBME and sustaining accountable professional practice. © 2026 British Educational Research Association.

title: Generative Humanoid Avatar Creation for Ethnicity-Focused Virtual Reality Studies
venue: 2026 12th International Conference on Virtual Reality, ICVR 2026
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic accelerated the shift of professional interactions meetings, collaborations, and workplace engagements into virtual environments. As people increasingly represented themselves through avatars, limited customization options undermined authentic self-representation, particularly for individuals from diverse ethnic backgrounds, reducing the sense of embodiment and inclusion. This gap motivated the present study, which investigates how workers perceive and respond to virtual colleagues varying in ethnicity, gender, and age within simulated professional settings. To enable this inquiry, we developed an end-to-end generative pipeline converting natural language prompts into customizable, animatable 3D humanoid avatars using text-to-image synthesis, TRELLIS-based 3D reconstruction, and automated skeletal rigging via Adobe Mixamo. An exploratory user study (N = 25) examined representational patterns and attitudinal responses across ten workplace scenarios. Descriptive analyses revealed scenario-conditioned clustering of perceived ethnicity and variation in collaboration willingness. A Scheirer-Ray-Hare test identified a significant main effect of professional scenario on collaboration intent, while perceived ethnicity alone did not reach significance. These findings suggest contextual role framing shapes collaboration responses more strongly than ethnicity, highlighting the need to jointly examine generative AI representation and human perception in fair, inclusive virtual workplaces. © 2026 IEEE.

To enable this inquiry, we developed an end-to-end generative pipeline converting natural language prompts into customizable, animatable 3D humanoid avatars using text-to-image synthesis, TRELLIS-based 3D reconstruction, and automated skeletal rigging via Adobe Mixamo. An exploratory user study (N = 25) examined representational patterns and attitudinal responses across ten workplace scenarios. Descriptive analyses revealed scenario-conditioned clustering of perceived ethnicity and variation in collaboration willingness. A Scheirer-Ray-Hare test identified a significant main effect of professional scenario on collaboration intent, while perceived ethnicity alone did not reach significance. These findings suggest contextual role framing shapes collaboration responses more strongly than ethnicity, highlighting the need to jointly examine generative AI representation and human perception in fair, inclusive virtual workplaces.  © 2026 IEEE.

title: Generative Placemaking: Co-creation of Cultural Memory Through a Collaborative Augmented Reality Narrative System in Foshan Historic Districts
venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science
abstract: Most digital cultural heritage applications still follow a “content-overlay” AR paradigm, superimposing predefined information onto physical sites for presentation and guided tours. This limits the narrative potential of physical media and constrains public agency in meaning-making. While prior work improves scene visualization and immersive tours, narratives remain expert-defined and hard to scale for open collaboration. To enable co-creative heritage storytelling, we designed and evaluated “Dynamic Mosaic,” a collaborative AR narrative system, and propose a generative placemaking interaction framework coupling “content generation—place experience—public participation.” Traditional mosaic craft was translated into a computational cultural interface as both spatial anchor and semantic base. In our experiment, physical mosaics triggered virtual characters, while participants uploaded images, texts, and story fragments; AIGC extended regionally grounded narratives that were assembled into dynamic semantic networks on a shared interface. Following a design science research paradigm, we recruited 80 participants (40 pairs; 48 female, 32 male; mean age 24.7, SD 3.5) for a simulation study with three conditions: physical-only (26), pure AR (26), and hybrid (28). Linear mixed-effects modeling showed the hybrid condition significantly outperformed single-media conditions in cultural learning, collaboration quality, and sense of place, yielding ~30% higher collaboration quality with no added cognitive load. Behavioral analysis further revealed spontaneous content re-creation beyond assigned tasks. We contribute a validated generative placemaking framework integrating traditional craft, AIGC, and AR, an experimental pipeline for collaborative narrative generation, and design evidence for transforming historic urban spaces into sustainable citizen-participatory digital cultural platforms. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.

title: GenerativeSurface: GenAI-Assisted Semantic Scaffolding for 3D Conceptual Design in Mixed Reality
venue: IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics
abstract: The transition from conceptual sketch to 3D model poses a major challenge in engineering design. While Mixed Reality (MR) enables direct 3D creation, designers face two key challenges: the Initiation Challenge (lack of meaningful starting points) and the Expression Challenge (difficulty in precise mid-air sketching). We introduce GenerativeSurface, leveraging AI to translate natural language descriptions into interactive 3D surfaces that aid designers in 3D sketching, simultaneously addressing both challenges. Our system transforms the design workflow into a fluid describe, generate, sketch, iterate cycle. Comparative evaluation against primitive scaffolding and freehand mid-air sketching demonstrates that our approach effectively bridges the gap between designers' conceptual intent and 3D sketch expression in immersive environments. © 1995-2012 IEEE.

title: GENIE: Generative Narrative Immersion Engine for Deep Reading Engagement
venue: Proceedings - 2026 IEEE Conference on Virtual Reality and 3D User Interfaces Abstracts and Workshops, VRW 2026
abstract: This paper presents GENIE (Generative Narrative Immersion Engine), a virtual reality (VR)-based reading system that generates story-adaptive 360° panoramic environments from narrative text to deepen readers' engagement with fictional stories. To this end, an AI pipeline segments book text into scene-level units, derives location-focused image prompts via large language models, and synthesizes corresponding panoramas using diffusion-based image generation and neural super-resolution models. In a within-subject user study (N=32) comparing this dynamic environment to a static baseline, we analyzed both subjective Story World Absorption (SWAS) and objective behavior (reading speed, head rotation). The results show that our story-adaptive reading system significantly increased transportation and mental imagery. Moreover, our study reveals critical interaction effects between the narrative and generated environments. These findings suggest that while generative VR can deepen absorption, its effectiveness is modulated by the visual concreteness and pacing of the source text, offering new design implications for the future of immersive reading experiences. © 2026 IEEE.

title: GenTouchVR: Generating a Touchable Virtual Reality Environment from a Single Image
venue: IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics
abstract: Creating interactive VR content typically requires extensive modeling effort, making scalable production difficult. We present an automated computational pipeline that converts a single image into an interactive 3D scene with plausible kinesthetic feedback. Our approach leverages a Large Language Model (LLM) to detect objects in the image and infer haptic properties from visual and textual cues. These extracted results are then utilized to synthesize 3D models and optimize haptic properties for perceptual distinguishability, while combining them into a complete interactive environment. A user study shows that the generated VR scenes provide compelling visuo-haptic experiences, highlighting the potential of our method for scalable multisensory world generation. To our knowledge, this is the first system to automatically produce VR scenes with force feedback from a single image, pointing toward a practical direction for lowering the barriers to creating haptically enriched VR content. © 1995-2012 IEEE.

title: GeoSceneGraph: Geometric Scene Graph Diffusion Model for Text-guided 3D Indoor Scene Synthesis
venue: ISPRS Annals of the Photogrammetry, Remote Sensing and Spatial Information Sciences
abstract: Methods that synthesize indoor 3D scenes from text prompts have wide-ranging applications in film production, interior design, video games, virtual reality, and synthetic data generation for training embodied agents. Existing approaches typically either train generative models from scratch or leverage vision-language models (VLMs). While VLMs achieve strong performance, particularly for complex or open-ended prompts, smaller task-specific models remain necessary for deployment on resource-constrained devices such as extended reality (XR) glasses or mobile phones. However, many generative approaches that train from scratch overlook the inherent graph structure of indoor scenes, which can limit scene coherence and realism. Conversely, methods that incorporate scene graphs either demand a user-provided semantic graph, which is generally inconvenient and restrictive, or rely on ground-truth relationship annotations, limiting their capacity to capture more varied object interactions. To address these challenges, we introduce GeoSceneGraph, a method that synthesizes 3D scenes from text prompts by leveraging the graph structure and geometric symmetries of 3D scenes, without relying on predefined relationship classes. Despite not using ground-truth relationships, GeoSceneGraph achieves performance comparable to methods that do. Our model is built on Equivariant Graph Neural Networks (EGNNs), but existing EGNN approaches are typically limited to low-dimensional conditioning and are not designed to handle complex modalities such as text. We propose a simple and effective strategy for conditioning EGNNs on text features, and we validate our design through ablation studies. © 2026 Copernicus GmbH. All rights reserved.

title: GestuProp: 3D Virtual Reality Prop Generation with Co-Speech Gestures
venue: Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems - Proceedings
abstract: Virtual Reality (VR) has been widely adopted in domains such as gaming, education, and healthcare, where 3D props play a central role in enabling immersive interaction. With the advancement of generative AI, 3D props can now be created rapidly; however, little research has explored how gestures and speech can be integrated to support prop generation. To address this gap, we introduce GestuProp, a VR prop generation system driven by co-speech gestures. Building on a formative study with 30 participants, we proposed a gesture design space and developed the VR system GestuProp. We then conducted a user study with 14 participants, which showed that GestuProp demonstrates good usability and favorable user experiences, while also revealing how object categories influence gesture use and interaction. These findings highlight the potential of gesture-speech synergy to advance prop generation in VR. © 2026 Copyright held by the owner/author(s).

title: GPS Effect: When Attentional Guiding is Detrimental to Learning
venue: Journal of Interactive Learning Research
abstract: This study examines the effects of step-by-step attentional guidance during immersive virtual reality (VR) lesson. While such guidance can enhance task completion, it may simultaneously facilitate or impede learners’ development of deep task understanding. In addition, the study evaluates the role of enactment, a generative learning strategy, in promoting meaningful learning outcomes following the VR lesson. Ninety-two master’s students in engineering received instruction on a manufacturing process through an instructional scenario and video before participating in the VR lesson. Results indicate that attentional guidance can have contrasting effects depending on whether enactment is subsequently employed, particularly regarding procedural knowledge acquisition. These findings suggest that step-by-step guidance may hinder procedural knowledge development—analogous to a GPS directing users along predetermined steps without encouraging contextual understanding—whereas incorporating an enactment phase after guided VR instruction appears to enhance procedural learning. © 2026, Association for the Advancement of Computing in Education. All rights reserved.

title: Greenery Alone Is Not Enough: Developing a Quantified Model of the Built Environment for Restorative Campuses Using AI-Driven VR and EEG
venue: Journal of Urban Planning and Development
abstract: While greenery is often associated with cognitive restoration, this study demonstrates that it alone may not be sufficient to optimize neurocognitive recovery in academic environments. Using ecologically validated virtual reality (VR) environments developed through artificial intelligence (AI)-driven generative modeling (Skybox AI Model 3.1; procedural and diffusion-based rendering) and electroencephalography (EEG)-based neurophysiological assessments, we explore how the composition of built and natural elements alongside higher-order spatial constructs like prospect, refuge, and novelty influences restoration. Cognitive restoration was indexed using normalized alpha brainwave (NAB) activity, a relative measure of alpha power commonly associated with relaxed wakefulness and mental recovery. Stepwise multiple regression models were employed to test two hypotheses. Model 1 examined the influence of macro built environment variables (BEVs), operationalized as visual percentage compositions of buildings, greenery, water, and visible sky within 360° panoramic views on NAB activity. These BEVs were manipulated in VR individually and in combination, and their intensification was quantified using visual area coverage. The model explained 64.5% of the variance in NAB (adjusted R2 = 0.645, p < 0.001), with greenery (standardized β = 9.009) contributing most positively, although its effects plateaued with intensification. Built structures (standardized β = 8.738), typically considered detrimental, were found to enhance NAB when spatially balanced with sky openness (β = 4.193), water features (β = 3.641), and environmental variation, suggesting a design-dependent restorative effect. Model 2 assessed the role of higher-order spatial constructs: prospect, refuge, environmental novelty, and overall environmental category quantified through expert evaluations of perceptual cues, spatial enclosure, and uncommon design patterns. This model accounted for 67.7% of the variance in NAB (adjusted R2 = 0.677, p < 0.001), with novelty (standardized β = 0.517) outweighing the influence of individual physical variables. Rather than offering a binary green versus built narrative, the study proposes a predictive framework for restorative academic design based on an optimized interplay of physical and perceptual variables. By integrating EEG data with AI-driven spatial simulations, this research contributes to evidence-based campus planning, suggesting that cognitive restoration emerges not solely from greenery, but from a compositional harmony of built and natural features, balanced prospect-refuge dynamics, and perceptual novelty. © 2026 American Society of Civil Engineers.

title: GSAC-D: Integrating Diffusion Models into Gaussian Splatting Avatar Creation for Flexible 3D Customization
venue: 2026 12th International Conference on Virtual Reality, ICVR 2026
abstract: Photorealistic avatars are vital for immersive Virtual and Augmented Reality (VR/AR), enabling realistic digital embodiment. Yet, most existing avatar generation methods produce static, single-outfit models that lack flexibility. In real-world VR/AR applications, users often need avatars that can adapt clothing or style across diverse social, professional, and training scenarios. Reconstructing new avatars for each appearance is costly and time-consuming, limiting personalization and scalability. Meanwhile, recent diffusion and language models have revolutionized 2D image editing through natural-language control, but extending these advances to 3D avatars remains difficult due to multi-view inconsistency and missing rigging information. As VR/AR applications expand into education, healthcare, and remote collaboration, the inability to customize photorealistic avatars in real time is becoming a critical bottleneck. To overcome these challenges, we introduce GSAC-D, a diffusion-driven framework that bridges 2D text-guided human image editing with 3D photorealistic, animatable avatar reconstruction. GSAC-D customizes Gaussian Splatting avatars from a single text prompt while ensuring cross-view coherence and preserving rigging integrity. It enables fully animatable, language-driven customization within 20 minutes - without requiring additional data capture or manual intervention. Our results demonstrate that diffusion-based editing provides a practical and scalable solution for creating flexible, expressive, and context-aware photorealistic avatars, paving the way for next-generation VR/AR experiences that are both personalized and adaptive. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Hand to Mouth: Shifting the Bare-Minimum Accessibility Paradigm in XR Through Crip-Hacking and Crip-Aesthetics
venue: Ethics and Society
abstract: eXtended Reality (XR) technologies often embed ableist design assumptions, privileging hand-based interaction and vision-centric interfaces that presume a normative able-bodied user. As a result, many disabled people—including those with limited mobility or blindness—are excluded from the outset, with accessibility added only as an afterthought. We critique this dynamic through a critical disability studies lens, formulating the notion of a “bare-minimum accessibility paradigm”—a tendency to meet only minimal compliance requirements rather than rethinking access as a generative design concern. In response, we propose crip-hacking and crip-aesthetics as transformative frameworks for accessible XR design. Crip-hacking draws on disabled communities’ DIY technology adaptations while crip-aesthetics reimagines disability-centric creativity as a design asset. We illustrate these approaches through an autoethnographic account of an XR artwork co-created with disabled artists using mouth gestures. This case demonstrates how reimagining XR through disability experiences challenges entrenched ableist design norms and broadens the discourse at the nexus of disability theory, technology ethics, and inclusive design research. © The Author(s) 2026.

title: HarassGuard: Detecting Harassment Behaviors in Social Virtual Reality with Vision-Language Models
venue: IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics
abstract: Social Virtual Reality (VR) platforms provide immersive social experiences but also expose users to serious risks of online harassment. Existing safety measures are largely reactive, while proactive solutions that detect harassment behavior during an incident often depend on sensitive biometric data, raising privacy concerns. In this paper, we present HarassGuard, a vision-language model (VLM) based system that detects physical harassment in social VR using only visual input. We construct an IRB-approved harassment vision dataset, apply prompt engineering, and fine-tune VLMs to detect harassment behavior by considering contextual information in social VR. Experimental results demonstrate that HarassGuard achieves competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art baselines (i.e., LSTM/CNN, Transformer), reaching an accuracy of up to 88.09% in binary classification and 68.85% in multi-class classification. Notably, HarassGuard matches these baselines while using significantly fewer fine-tuning samples (200 vs. 1,115), offering unique advantages in contextual reasoning and privacy-preserving detection. © 1995-2012 IEEE.

title: Harnessing large language models for virtual reality exploration testing: a case study
venue: Automated Software Engineering
abstract: As the Virtual Reality (VR) industry expands, the need for automated GUI testing is growing rapidly. Large Language Models (LLMs), capable of retaining information long-term and analyzing both visual and textual data, are emerging as a potential key to deciphering the complexities of VR’s evolving user interfaces. In this paper, we conduct a case study to investigate the capability of using LLMs, particularly GPT-4o, for field of view (FOV) analysis in VR exploration testing. Specifically, we validate that LLMs can identify test entities in FOVs and that prompt engineering can effectively enhance the accuracy of test entity identification from to. Our study also shows that LLMs can accurately describe identified entities’ features with at least a accuracy rate. We further find out that the core features that effectively represent an entity are color, placement, and shape. Furthermore, the combination of the three features can especially be used to improve the accuracy of determining identical entities in multiple FOVs with the highest F1-score of. Additionally, our study demonstrates that LLMs are capable of scene recognition and spatial understanding in VR with precisely designed structured prompts. Finally, we find that LLMs fail to label the identified test entities, and we discuss potential solutions as future research directions. © The Author(s) 2025.

Additionally, our study demonstrates that LLMs are capable of scene recognition and spatial understanding in VR with precisely designed structured prompts. Finally, we find that LLMs fail to label the identified test entities, and we discuss potential solutions as future research directions. © The Author(s) 2025.

title: Harnessing large language models in virtual CBT for university students' academic anxiety: a preliminary randomized trial
venue: Frontiers in public health
abstract: Academic anxiety is a common mental health problem among university students. It is often associated with reduced learning efficiency and an increased risk of depression. Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is supported by an established evidence base, but its use in university settings is still limited by factors such as therapist availability, time, and physical space. To explore a new approach to digitally assisted intervention, this study integrated virtual reality (VR), large language model (LLM), and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) technologies. We developed an LLM-VR-CBT system based on CBT principles and preliminarily examined its short-term intervention effects on academic anxiety among university students. This study used a three-arm randomized controlled design. A total of 60 university students with academic anxiety were included and randomly assigned to the LLM-VR-CBT group, traditional CBT group, or minimal-support control group, with 20 participants in each group. The intervention lasted 4 weeks. The linear mixed-effects model results showed significant group-by-time interactions for academic anxiety and heart rate. The LLM-VR-CBT group and traditional CBT group showed significantly greater reductions in academic anxiety and heart rate than the minimal-support control group. The difference in change between the two active intervention groups did not reach statistical significance. Skin temperature did not show a significant group-by-time interaction. These findings suggest that the LLM-VR-CBT system may help reduce academic anxiety among university students in the short term. Because this was a small, short-term exploratory trial and adverse events were not systematically collected as prespecified safety endpoints, future studies with larger samples, multicenter designs, long-term follow-up, and predefined safety monitoring are needed to further evaluate the system's stability, safety, feasibility, and application boundaries. title: HawkerVerse: Crafting Immersive Singapore Hawker Heritage Experiences through Multisensory Virtual Reality and Large Language Models
venue: ICHEC 2025 - Adjunct Proceedings of the International Conference on Human-Engaged Computing
abstract: We present HawkerVerse, a multisensory virtual reality (VR) system that supports immersive Singapore hawker cultural heritage experiences through embodied interaction. Using Newton Food Centre as a case study, we developed a system that integrates virtual architectural hawker environments, an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven conversational agent, and a haptic-olfactory interface to recreate the sensory and social dimensions of hawker life. Users can explore the virtual hawker centre via natural locomotion, converse with an AI agent powered by a local large language model (LLM), and experience realistic haptic and olfactory feedback related to representative hawker foods, such as laksa, prawn noodles, and Hainanese chicken rice. HawkerVerse demonstrates how multimodal feedback and context-aware AI can support interactive cultural learning and embodied heritage interaction in virtual environments. © 2025 Copyright held by the owner/author(s).

title: HINT: A Bayesian RAG-LAM Framework for Real-Time Semantic Communication in XR Services
venue: IEEE Communications Magazine
abstract: Immersive extended reality (XR) is a key 6G use case, but its ultra-high bandwidth and milli-second latency requirements clash with the high inference cost of large AI models (LAMs). These models enable semantic communication by inferring user intent from multimodal signals and transmitting only task-relevant information, yet their computation time creates an intelligence latency paradox. This article introduces HINT (Hierarchical Intent-aware Network for XR Transmission), a tutorial system-oriented framework that explains how to implement a Bayesian retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipeline for XR. HINT decomposes cognition into a fast edge tier (System 1) and a slower cloud tier (System 2). At the edge, a low-latency cognitive reflex arc uses Bayesian RAG over a compact intent knowledge base to handle frequent, high-confidence interactions. An uncertainty trigger decides when an input is too ambiguous and must be escalated to a cloud-hosted large model for deeper reasoning. We outline design decisions, including the intent vector structure, the organization and update of the edge knowledge base, and the mapping from intent to asymmetric transmission and rendering policies for 3D Gaussian splatting scenes. Simulation results in a Unity-based XR environment indicate that HINT can reduce bandwidth and client-side load while keeping intent latency within interactive bounds. We conclude with open challenges and practical guidelines for deploying Bayesian RAG at the edge in future 6G-native XR systems. © 1979-2012 IEEE.

title: Holodeck: Case Studies in Exploring AI Use in Automatic VR World Generation
venue: Springer Proceedings in Business and Economics
abstract: Recent advancements in AI, particularly through transformer and diffusion architectures, have unlocked possibilities once considered science fiction, such as generating 3D objects from simple prompts and creating interactive avatars capable of dynamic responses and role-playing. This paper presents three case studies examining different workflows for leveraging the context of objects or avatars to assign specific properties, with the vision of enabling the development of immersive applications within LLM-powered virtual environments. The case studies explore how object properties, such as scale and relational position, can be defined and how agent-driven avatars can reflect their capabilities and select animations, while outlining challenges for future developers, including refining prompt design for conciseness and inference speed, diversifying output types, and establishing objective evaluation methods. Using the open-source Holodeck project as a basis, these concepts are demonstrated through three case studies: one on object scaling, animations, and reflective behaviors of a teaching assistant avatar, and finally a workflow and LLM benchmark for exploring objects’ relational properties to each other. This work aims to highlight the potential for integrating contextual properties into generated virtual worlds, allowing non-expert practitioners to help build VR applications in the future. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.

title: How does Artificial Intelligence (AI) change in Nursing Education?
venue: ICEMT 2025 - 2025 9th International Conference on Education and Multimedia Technology
abstract: The term "artificial intelligence (AI)"was first emerged in 1956 during a workshop defined as "science and engineering of making intelligent machines, especially intelligent computer programs". The use of artificial intelligence (AI) in health education has a significant impact on clinical practice, research, and policy. The integrations of artificial intelligence (AI) technology including the natural language processing (NLP), machine learning (ML) and generative pre-trained transformers (GPT), have the potential to advance nursing education contents and processes. The aim of this study is to study and discuss the integration of AI in nursing education as the framework for identifying the opportunities and challenges associated with high-quality nursing in teaching, clinical practice, and research. AI in nursing education framework involves curriculum design, teaching and learning analysis, content and clinical scenario recommendation, chatbots and simulation, automatic assessment and marking system. Intelligent nursing tutoring system. The future of nursing education will inherently embrace AI-driven applications and technologies. "AI nursing systems"hold significant importance in the future. Ultimately, equipping future nursing educators with proficiency in AI technologies and associated ethical implications are essential for promoting high-quality nursing practice and education. © 2025 Copyright held by the owner/author(s).

title: Human-Agent Trust Mediation: Augmented Context Understanding as a Method to Dynamically Calibrate Machine-Reliance in Emergency Response
venue: CEUR Workshop Proceedings
abstract: The combination of extended Reality (XR) with conversational AI is emerging as a situational awareness (SA) augmentation layer for Emergency First Responders (EFRs), where stress, uncertainty, and time pressure degrade spatial reasoning and decision-making. Current approaches in conversational AI powered by spatial vision language models (S-VLMs) enable reliable SA support like a robot reporting metrically-grounded distances of detected real-world objects, e.g., "The car is 10 meters away.", to mitigate error-prone human distance estimations. This process constitutes a static human-agent trust relation that has the potential risk of causing over-reliance in EFRs. What happens if the robot’s distance measurement is wrong because of light conditions? or if there is a hidden combustion inside the car? Therefore, we argue toward calibrated trust, including real-time trust measurement in machine-report, accounting for unexpected events, and interface strategies that respond to over and under trust as they emerge, e.g., "The car is estimated at 10 meters away with 65% confidence giving the light conditions." or "The car is now 5 meters away and a crackling sound is detected near the same location, careful for potential hidden combustion." Building on our prior prototype demonstrating that ground-truth depth injected into a VLM improves distance judgments and SA in an XR-robotic EFR scenario, we argue that the next iteration must steer spatial context understanding toward conversational agentic trusting: a robot teammate that actively explores, detects dynamic hazards (e.g., structural instability), and communicates changing threat trajectories grounded in multimodal evidence (e.g., depth, audio, thermal cues). We contribute (1) a measurement method for modeling trust in real time under pressure using behavioral, attentional, system, and psychophysiological signals; and (2) actionable XR interface principles for dynamically calibrating reliance, preventing automation misuse, and preserving human authority. © 2026 Copyright for this paper by its authors.

title: Human-AI Co-Creative Aesthetics: Mechanisms and Value of Deep Learning Image Generation in Art Education
venue: Proceedings of the 2nd International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Interaction Design
abstract: The deep integration of generative artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping the paradigm of artistic creation, transforming “human-AI co-creation” from a technological possibility into a critical issue that art education must address. Based on theoretical reasoning and literature synthesis, this study systematically reviews cutting-edge theories of human-AI co-creativity and constructs a five-stage co-creative model encompassing “Divergent Exploration - Intent Articulation - Co-generative Exploration - Critical Curation - Iterative Refinement.” Integrating Jeongki Lim's theory of “relational artifacts,” Duri Long's framework of “co-creative AI,” and recent systematic review findings, the study elucidates the intrinsic mechanisms of human-AI co-creation from the dual perspectives of relational construction and interaction design. The findings reveal that human-AI co-creation is fundamentally a deep collaborative relationship characterized by “human-led, AI-enhanced” dynamics: AI expands the possibility space of creativity, while humans remain the ultimate agents of intention setting, value judgment, and meaning construction. The “imperfections” of AI-generated images are transformed into creative resources through mechanisms of “serendipity capture,” “critical awareness against over-compliance,” and “metacognitive reflection in intention-output gaps.” This transformation is reshaping the value structure of art education, shifting it from an exclusive focus on “skill training” toward the multidimensional integration of “creative cultivation,” “narrative capacity,” and “aesthetic competence.” Based on these findings, this paper proposes collaborative teaching strategies for future-oriented art education.
