title: Human-Centered Human–AI Interaction for Wearable and Extended Reality Creative Systems: Implications for Industry and Education in Korea
venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science
abstract: This study proposes a human-centered content development methodology for investigating how humans can effectively understand, control, and creatively collaborate with generative artificial intelligence (AI) systems in wearable computing and extended reality (XR)-based media environments. With AI transitioning from a production-oriented tool to a cognitive collaborator, the emphasis of creative systems shifts from automation to human competence—specifically how designers, educators, and creators refine their interactions with AI for greater creative intelligence, contextual awareness, and emotional depth. The proposed methodology introduces a three-phase framework comprising Human Understanding and Intent Modeling, AI-driven Generation and Adaptation, and XR Output Realization, focusing on human interpretive control and iterative feedback to guide and reshape AI-generated outputs. The framework is explored through scenario-based creative tasks and task-oriented activities, complemented by semi-structured interviews in which participants engage in representative text and image generation tasks situated within wearable and XR co-creation scenarios. These scenarios reflect interdisciplinary applications in cultural storytelling, multimedia production, and interactive XR installations using AI-enabled smart glasses and immersive interfaces. Qualitative analysis of participant responses and task outcomes suggests that the proposed approach supports AI interpretability, multimodal fluency, and embodied decision-making, contributing to more expressive, emotionally resonant, and contextually adaptive creative processes compared to automation-centric workflows. This study contributes to the emerging field of human–AI collaborative design by reframing wearable and XR systems as intelligent creative instruments and providing a methodological and educational foundation for training future creators to engage with AI as a collaborative partner that extends human imagination. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.

title: Human-in-the-Loop Rebar Inspection: Integrating Vision Foundation Model with Mixed Reality for Construction Quality Assurance
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Human-Machine Systems, ICHMS 2026
abstract: Rebar spacing must be precisely laid out before concrete is poured, yet current inspection relies on tape-measure readings, which are slow, error-prone, and leave no digital record. Automated computer-vision methods improve throughput but remain vulnerable to site clutter, and confine inspectors to screen-based workflows detached from the physical structure. This paper presents a human-in-the-loop Mixed Reality (MR) inspection framework that pairs a domain-adapted Segment Anything Model 3 (SAM3) with the Microsoft HoloLens 2. The system captures a rebar scene, segments each bar in real time, and maps the resulting 2D contours into 3D world coordinates via raycasting. Inspectors select any two rebars by air-tap gesture; the spacing is computed automatically and displayed as a holographic overlay anchored to the physical bars. Across 25 spacing pairs and 75 measurements on a controlled rebar mockup, the system achieved a mean relative error of 2.52% (95% CI 2.46%-2.58%) and and end-to-end latency of 2.8 s, confirming suitability for on-site quality control. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Hybrid GAn-Based Low-Latency Compression Technique for 6G Communication
venue: Proceedings of the 3rd International Conference on Innovations in Cybersecurity and Data Science, ICICDS 2026
abstract: Sixth-generation wireless networks are required to enable real-time holographic communication as well as augmented reality and virtual reality applications. This enables ultra-high data rates and sub-millisecond latency. These applications generate massive volumes of volumetric and high-resolution 3D data with multi-view. Conventional codecs like H.265/HEVC introduce computational delay though it provides high compression efficiency. Superior quality can be provided through deep learningbased compression techniques but they fail to satisfy latency constraints. This work presents a hybrid compression method combining H.265/HEVC baseline encoding with Generative Adversarial Network. These are kept at edge computing nodes. Evaluation results indicate enhanced compression ratio, decreased bit error rate, and reduced latency. Further, this technique is compared to standalone traditional and AI-based methods. This proposed study is applicable for real-time holographic and sixth generation communication systems. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Hydroverse education: an AI-assisted education framework for immersive learning and training environments
venue: Journal of Hydroinformatics
abstract: Hydroinformatics education has been constrained by pedagogical approaches that fail to convey the complexity of water systems. Virtual Reality (VR) offers a transformative solution through interactive and experiential learning. This study introduces HydroVerse Education, an immersive virtual classroom integrating VR and artificial intelligence to modernize hydroinformatics education. Using Unreal Engine, Metahuman, and Generative AI, the platform creates an interactive environment with immersive communication and knowledge generation. An AI-driven virtual instructor enables real-time voice-based interactions providing personalized guidance for diverse learning styles. HydroVerse Education enhances engagement through realistic simulations of complex hydroinformatics scenarios, bridging theory and practice. Addressing the need for accessible, cost-effective educational tools, the platform offers flexible, adaptive learning experiences for instructors, and researchers. This study details the system's development, architecture, and capabilities, while discussing challenges and future directions for VR integration in education. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Igniting Heritage: A Framework for AI-Enhanced XR Documentary Design of Chinese Fire-Based ICH Performances
venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science
abstract: Chinese fire-based Intangible Cultural Heritage (ICH), such as the vigorous “Fire Qilin” dances, faces a profound paradox: its cultural power is rooted in the visceral, dangerous, and ephemeral nature of live fire, yet these very attributes accelerate its decline. Prevailing digital preservation methods, predominantly two-dimensional video, fail to capture the multisensory, embodied, and spatially-grounded essence of such rituals, often reducing them to passive spectacles. This paper argues for a paradigm shift from archival replication to empathetic, narrative-driven re-living. We propose and demonstrate a practical pathway that synergizes XR Virtual Production and Generative AI to create culturally resonant narrative films. Grounded in the Digital Humanities principles of cultural empathy and experiential authenticity, our two-stage workflow involves: 1) Cultural Sensing and Controlled Field Building, using XR stages to safely reconstruct ritual performances within authentic digital settings; and 2) Generative Augmentation and Narrative Synthesis, where AI-generated visual elements (e.g., digital fireworks) are created under community guidance to amplify cultural meaning, followed by cinematic storytelling. Through a case study of the “Dongchong Fire Qilin,” we produced a short film that was validated by the inheritor Master Mai as shocking and spectacular, confirming it captured the tradition’s true spirit. This work contributes a validated, humanistic approach to digital heritage, showcasing how virtual production and generative AI can serve as powerful tools for creative fidelity and sustainable cultural transmission, while critically engaging with the ethics of narrative sovereignty and digital interpretation. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.

Grounded in the Digital Humanities principles of cultural empathy and experiential authenticity, our two-stage workflow involves: 1) Cultural Sensing and Controlled Field Building, using XR stages to safely reconstruct ritual performances within authentic digital settings; and 2) Generative Augmentation and Narrative Synthesis, where AI-generated visual elements (e.g., digital fireworks) are created under community guidance to amplify cultural meaning, followed by cinematic storytelling. Through a case study of the “Dongchong Fire Qilin,” we produced a short film that was validated by the inheritor Master Mai as shocking and spectacular, confirming it captured the tradition’s true spirit. This work contributes a validated, humanistic approach to digital heritage, showcasing how virtual production and generative AI can serve as powerful tools for creative fidelity and sustainable cultural transmission, while critically engaging with the ethics of narrative sovereignty and digital interpretation. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.

title: Image-to-3D for Cultural Heritage: Voice Interaction and Retrieval-Augmented Guidance in VR
venue: Proceedings - 2026 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and eXtended and Virtual Reality, AIxVR 2026
abstract: Virtual museum visits have an ever-growing collection due to the high demand for the digitization of historically, artistically, and culturally significant artifacts. This demand is growing even more with the popularization of Virtual Reality (VR) technology, which requires immersive and interactive experiences to motivate users to move from mere spectators to active participants. In this context, this work proposes an end-to-end approach to create a custom and interactive VR experiences through virtual exhibitions. Using a single image, artifacts from real museum exhibitions are generated and assembled into a virtual museum, enabling customized and interactive VR experiences. In addition, the museum is voice-controlled, allowing users to manipulate its display in real time, and a retrieval-augmented generation technique is employed to provide grounded, object-scoped explanations. In an initial analysis, an evaluation was performed using the LLM-as-judge protocol to analyze the quality of the reconstructions. Overall, our study demonstrated promising results in making virtual tours even more immersive and educational, creating an interactive environment and enriching the experience. © 2026 IEEE.

title: IMERSIVA: Virtual Reality System for High Impact Teaching Strategies
venue: 2026 IEEE Conference on Serious Games and Applications for Health (SeGAH)
abstract: This paper presents "Imersiva,"an integrated system designed to enhance English language conversation practice through the synergy of Virtual Reality (VR), Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI), and real-time pedagogical monitoring. While traditional methods often struggle with student anxiety and lack of immersion, "Imersiva"utilizes a service-oriented architecture to connect VR scenarios, such as a fruit market and a restaurant, with Large Language Models (LLMs) like Gemini 2.5 flash and GPT-5 mini. The system enables authentic, low-anxiety interactions with virtual agents while providing educators with a web-based dashboard for classroom orchestration. Preliminary results from usability and efficacy tests conducted with 15 participants, using a pre-test and post-test methodology, demonstrate significant improvements in conversational confidence and engagement. Evaluation through the System Usability Scale (SUS) yielded high scores, confirming the platform's intuitive design and its potential as a high-impact teaching tool. These findings suggest that the integration of immersive XR environments and intelligent conversational agents can effectively bridge the gap in oral practice within the educational sphere. © 2026 IEEE.

title: ImmersiProtor: A Collaborative Mixed-Prototype Tool Integrating Spatial Augmented Reality and Component-layered Generation
venue: Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems - Proceedings
abstract: Conceptual design is a critical stage in product development, which is a co-design process involving multidisciplinary collaboration based on prototypes. In this paper, we aim to propose a novel prototype paradigm that combines the distinct strengths of generative artificial intelligence (GAI) and spatial augmented reality (SAR), leveraging the expressive potential of SAR and the creative potential of GAI for co-design. To achieve this, we initially conducted a formative study with designers to explore how these technologies could be effectively combined to facilitate co-design. Based on our findings, we introduce ImmersiProtor, a prototype tool integrating multi-view SAR and component-layered GAI for co-design. On one hand, ImmersiProtor allows design team members to freely create and modify physical prototypes while automatically generating multi-view and high-fidelity renderings that are projected onto the surfaces of the physical prototype using SAR technology, enabling immersive communication and intuitive evaluation. On the other hand, ImmersiProtor introduces a component-layered generation and collaboration mode, offering both personal and shared team component resources. It ensures that individual team members can explore ideas independently without interference, while also supporting concept integration, evaluation, and iteration. We implemented ImmersiProtor, which involves a web-based application and an SAR design space. We conducted a user study to verify ImmersiProtor's usability in supporting prototype and collaboration. Our results highlighted ImmersiProtor's inherent strengths in enhancing intuition, promoting collaboration, and strengthening GAI controllability. We also explored the effect of mixed interaction on design and critically discuss its best practices for the HCI community. © 2026 Copyright held by the owner/author(s).

title: Immersive cognitive factory twin: optimizing industry 5.0 with an integrated VR, ML, and LLM framework
venue: Production and Manufacturing Research
abstract: Optimizing modern factories requires dynamic, data-driven decision support aligned with Industry 5.0’s human-centric principles. This research introduces the ‘immersive cognitive factory twin’, a novel framework leveraging virtual reality (VR), machine learning (ML), and large language models (LLMs) to enhance key performance indicators (KPIs). The system features an immersive VR simulation for visualizing factory operations, a neural network trained on simulated data to predict KPIs (e.g. operator success rate), and an integrated LLM to analyze predictions and suggest actionable improvements (e.g. operator reassignments, breaks) via natural language within the VR interface. A proof-of-concept multi-run simulation of a three-station assembly process demonstrated substantial advantages (throughput +28.6%, scrap −35.4%; t-tests and ANOVA, (Formula presented.)). This framework empowers managers with real-time, actionable insights for substantial gains in factory efficiency and resource optimization. © 2026 The Author(s). title: Immersive creativity: a framework for expressive and creative interaction in virtual and mixed reality inspired by musical thinking
venue: Frontiers in Virtual Reality
abstract: This paper proposes a novel framework for designing immersive creative systems in Virtual and Mixed Reality (VR/MR) by drawing upon the rich, centuries-old domain of music. It argues that the principles underlying musical creation provide a powerful blueprint for interaction design. By analyzing the cognitive processes of composition and performance, this work synthesizes a design framework organized around four key pillars: (1) the Visualization of the Sonic Space, which translates abstract musical ideas into navigable environments; (2) the design of Embodied Instruments as gestural interfaces; (3) the implementation of Structured Freedom through guiding constraints; and (4) a paradigm shift towards The Composer as World-Builder, creating environments for interpretation. The paper then demonstrates the framework's practical application by outlining its use in designing real-world immersive experiences. The goal is to guide development away from simple virtual tools and towards interpretive, collaborative environments that amplify human creative potential. title: Immersive Learning Environment Design of Outdoor Education Space Using Artificial Intelligence Augmented Reality Technology
venue: International Journal of Advanced Computer Science and Applications
abstract: This study presents a technically grounded design and implementation of an AI- and AR-enabled immersive learning environment for outdoor education. Moving beyond conceptual descriptions, the study develops an executable system framework that integrates adaptive navigation and positioning, context-aware virtual tours, task-driven scenario simulation, and real-time feedback mechanisms. Each functional module is explicitly linked to algorithmic implementations, including multi-sensor state estimation, constrained generative scene construction, and reinforcement-based adaptive control, enabling reproducible system behavior in real outdoor settings. A controlled field experiment was conducted using an experimental group and a control group under identical instructional conditions. Quantitative evaluation based on pre–post testing, behavioral logging, and statistical analysis demonstrates that the proposed system achieves statistically significant improvements in learning interest, participation, knowledge mastery, and problem-solving ability. Experimental conditions, data characteristics, and methodological limitations are explicitly reported to support result verification and generalizability. The findings indicate that the proposed immersive learning environment constitutes a validated system-level contribution rather than a purely conceptual framework, offering practical and scientific value for computer science–oriented educational technology research. © 2026, Science and Information Organization. title: Immersive Narrative Mechanism of Cultural Heritage Transmission Enabled by Generative Artificial Intelligence from the Perspective of Human-Machine Collaboration
venue: 2026 International Conference on Intelligent Engineering and Next-Gen Healthcare Systems (IEHNS)
abstract: This study proposes a human-AI collaborative framework to resolve the tension between technological innovation and depth of cultural transmission in heritage communication, exemplified through the intelligent dissemination of traditional Chinese tea culture. By integrating generative artificial intelligence and augmented reality, the framework employs a four-dimensional cultural genome indexing system spanning architectural, material, behavioral, and spiritual layers to enable progressive narrative exploration - from tea-ceremony utensils to ritual practices and philosophical principles. AR-driven virtual reconstruction of historical tea culture and large language model-enhanced dialogue interfaces transform passive consumption into dynamic co-creation, where users actively shape cultural meanings through natural language engagement. Self-optimizing mechanisms dynamically align technological outputs with the depth of cultural transmission by synthesizing multi-source feedback, user interactions, curator oversight, and ethical validation, thereby resolving the imbalance where technological spectacle overshadows substantive cultural transmission. Positioning AI as an amplifier of human expertise, the framework offers solutions for heritage preservation, harmonizing computational power with cultural intentionality to foster immersive, ethically grounded engagement. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Immersive Training Simulation: Exploring Two Narrative Approaches
venue: Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems
abstract: In high-stakes professions such as that of negotiators and pilots, simulations are frequently employed as a risk-free training tool to facilitate the refinement of skills and decision-making abilities. While traditional simulations are effective, they are resource-intensive. In contrast, computer-based simulations offer scalability but may lack realism and sensory engagement. This study examines the potential of mobile phones in simulation-based learning, with a particular focus on a 3D hostage-taking scenario designed to enhance immersion through realistic interactions. By integrating a detailed environment and interactive elements, this approach demonstrates the potential of mobile technology to enhance the realism and engagement of training. Furthermore, the emergence of Large Language Models (LLMs) has transformed digital narration by moving beyond the limitations of rigid, time-consuming conversational trees. The traditional methods, which required a considerable degree of multidisciplinary expertise, frequently resulted in disrupted dialogue coherence due to the constraints imposed on the pathways available for communication. However, LLMs enable the creation of dynamic virtual personas from simple descriptions, thereby streamlining content creation and enhancing immersion through their expansive conversational capabilities. This publication reports on a digital hostage-taking simulation that utilised both mobile phones for communication and LLMs for character simulation, thereby highlighting advancements in feasibility and immersion. © The Editor(s) (if applicable) and The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.

title: Immersive Virtual Reality Simulator with Real-Time AI-Based Evaluation for Improving Surgical Team Performance
venue: Proceedings - 2026 IEEE Conference on Virtual Reality and 3D User Interfaces Abstracts and Workshops, VRW 2026
abstract: Surgical Safety Checklist (SSC) consisting of Timeout and Debrief performed at appropriate time in the operating room (OR) has shown to be a critical and effective tool to reduce errors and improve patient safety. Simulation-based training of OR team members is critical for performing SSC but remains challenging using traditional methods. We have developed a VR simulator that utilizes the Operating Room Black Box (R) (ORBB) recordings, Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques and Large Language Models (LLM) to simulate and evaluate realistic scenarios. Virtual Humanoid Avatars representing surgical team members, allowed trainees to interact with and learn from scenarios derived directly from ORBB Recordings. Trainees' speech transcribed using Whisper AI were analyzed in real-time using LLM fined tuned with SSC assessment rubrics. We compared zero-shot LLM-based evaluations against ORBB grades using accuracy and F1-score. For Timeout, GPT-OSS 20B achieved 0.88 accuracy / 0.91 F1, and Gemma 3-27B 0.87 / 0.90. For Debrief, both models achieved 0.90 accuracy, with GPT-OSS slightly higher (0.92 F1) than Gemma (0.91 F 1). The results show that the VR simulator for training in SSC with automated assessment model using LLM is highly realistic, reliable and can be used for improving operating room team performance. © 2026 IEEE.

title: In-Class Flipped Classroom in VR Environments: The Trade-off between Knowledge Retention and Design Confidence
venue: 2026 8th International Conference on Computer Science and Technologies in Education, CSTE 2026
abstract: This study investigated the impact of a segmented in-class flipped model compared to a traditional pre-class flipped model on learning outcomes within an intellectual property design course integrated with high-immersion virtual reality. A quasi-experimental non-equivalent control group design was employed involving 33 undergraduate students majoring in digital media arts. Participants were assigned to either a traditional flipped classroom with 16 students or a segmented in-class flipped classroom with 17 students. Data were collected via assessments measuring knowledge retention and flow experience alongside cognitive load and design confidence. Results indicated a distinct pedagogical trade-off where the traditional group demonstrated superior consolidation of declarative knowledge while the inclass group experienced a marginal retention regression despite a stronger academic baseline. This phenomenon is termed performance inversion. The in-class group conversely reported significantly higher flow states. Furthermore a confidence reversal effect was observed where the experimental group overcame a lower baseline to achieve significantly higher post-task design confidence grounded in both visual decoding and process fluency. The findings suggest that high-immersion environments impose a retention tax on rote memory while paying a dividend in psychological engagement. Consequently instructional choice must align with specific educational objectives where traditional models suit terminology retention and segmented in-class models foster creative intuition and psychological readiness. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Information Technology for VR Training Evaluation with First Aid Skills Improvement to Detecting Human Resource Damage in Emergencies based on Behavioural Methods
venue: International Journal of Image, Graphics and Signal Processing
abstract: Traditional first aid preparation methods often fail to reproduce realistic stress levels and to simulate visual difficulty in identifying lesions in critical situations. In emergencies, delays in recognising injuries or errors in protocols result in critical losses of human resources. The use of computer graphics and virtual reality technologies enables you to create a safe yet highly realistic environment for rescuers to test and improve their skills. The article presents an integrated methodological framework for assessing the effectiveness of VR first-aid training in conditions of damage to civilian infrastructure. The main focus is on developing mathematical models and algorithms to identify and evaluate the quality of rescuers' actions by analysing digital interaction signals in a virtual environment. A composite efficiency indicator is proposed that combines normalised parameters for reaction time, manipulation accuracy, stress level, and immersion. The work aims to formalise a mathematical model to assess the effectiveness of VR training in developing skills for lesion identification and first aid provision, using quantitative metrics. The study aims to identify statistically significant differences in learning speed and skill retention between groups using VR simulations and traditional methods. The project aims to validate innovative content creation methods, including mobile photogrammetry, to visualise damaged infrastructure and victim models. The study used a comprehensive approach that includes mobile photogrammetry and generative neural networks to create a library of 3D assets with varying degrees of detail. Performance score is based on composite indicator that integrates normalised data on reaction time, manipulation accuracy, error count, immersion rate. Linear mixed models, exponential approximations, and bootstrap estimation of effect stability were used to analyse hierarchical data and individual learning trajectories. The experimental part includes the use of mobile photogrammetry and generative neural networks to create realistic 3D models of affected environments and identify types of injuries (bleeding, burns, unconsciousness). To analyse the dynamics of learning and maintaining skills, models with mixed effects and exponential forgetting curves are used. The results confirm that the use of VR technologies provides a statistically significant acceleration in the development of automated skills for lesion identification and assistance compared to traditional methods. The proposed approach is a scalable tool for preparing civil and rescue services to act in critical situations. Experimental data showed that the integral performance score in the VR group increased from 0.42 ± 0.10 to 0.76 ± 0.08, while in the control group it increased from only 0.40 ± 0.09 to 0.55 ± 0.10 (p < 0.001). The largest effect was observed in the bleeding arrest scenario, where the effect size (Cohen's d) reached 2.3. The analysis of forgetting curves confirmed the superiority of VR: the skill loss rate in the VR group was 0.25, providing knowledge retention 1.8 times longer than in the control group (0.45). The study confirmed that VR simulations significantly accelerate the formation of automated behaviour patterns and reduce reaction time in extreme conditions. The proposed mathematical assessment model provides objective feedback and standardisation of the rescue training process. The results indicate the high practical value of introducing such tools into training programs for civilian and military structures to minimise losses in real emergencies. © 2026, Modern Education and Computer Science Press. All rights reserved.

The work aims to formalise a mathematical model to assess the effectiveness of VR training in developing skills for lesion identification and first aid provision, using quantitative metrics. The study aims to identify statistically significant differences in learning speed and skill retention between groups using VR simulations and traditional methods. The project aims to validate innovative content creation methods, including mobile photogrammetry, to visualise damaged infrastructure and victim models. The study used a comprehensive approach that includes mobile photogrammetry and generative neural networks to create a library of 3D assets with varying degrees of detail. Performance score is based on composite indicator that integrates normalised data on reaction time, manipulation accuracy, error count, immersion rate. Linear mixed models, exponential approximations, and bootstrap estimation of effect stability were used to analyse hierarchical data and individual learning trajectories. The experimental part includes the use of mobile photogrammetry and generative neural networks to create realistic 3D models of affected environments and identify types of injuries (bleeding, burns, unconsciousness). To analyse the dynamics of learning and maintaining skills, models with mixed effects and exponential forgetting curves are used. The results confirm that the use of VR technologies provides a statistically significant acceleration in the development of automated skills for lesion identification and assistance compared to traditional methods. The proposed approach is a scalable tool for preparing civil and rescue services to act in critical situations. Experimental data showed that the integral performance score in the VR group increased from 0.42 ± 0.10 to 0.76 ± 0.08, while in the control group it increased from only 0.40 ± 0.09 to 0.55 ± 0.10 (p < 0.001). The largest effect was observed in the bleeding arrest scenario, where the effect size (Cohen's d) reached 2.3. The analysis of forgetting curves confirmed the superiority of VR: the skill loss rate in the VR group was 0.25, providing knowledge retention 1.8 times longer than in the control group (0.45). The study confirmed that VR simulations significantly accelerate the formation of automated behaviour patterns and reduce reaction time in extreme conditions. The proposed mathematical assessment model provides objective feedback and standardisation of the rescue training process. The results indicate the high practical value of introducing such tools into training programs for civilian and military structures to minimise losses in real emergencies. © 2026, Modern Education and Computer Science Press. title: Inkfinity: Augmenting Stylus-Based Handwriting with Contextual Awareness in AR
venue: Proceedings - 2026 IEEE Conference on Virtual Reality and 3D User Interfaces Abstracts and Workshops, VRW 2026
abstract: We present Inkfinity, an AR interaction paradigm bridging stylusbased spatial inking and actionable user intent through multimodal semantics. Using a spatially-tracked stylus, users write on physical surfaces and transform handwriting into interactive smart widgets via simple encircling gestures (e.g., converting 'Meeting at 3pm' into a tappable reminder). Beyond digitization, Inkfinity enables contextual spatial queries: users encircle real-world objects to trigger AI-generated insights as AR overlays. By combining fluid stylus input with intelligent semantic understanding, this work demonstrates a seamless workflow for augmenting productivity in everyday environments. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Innovative Application of Generative Adversarial Networks in User Interface Design
venue: Proceedings of the 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Interaction Design
abstract: To enhance the efficiency and innovation of user interface design, this study explores the application of Generative Adversarial Networks through adversarial training between the generator and discriminator models. The research covers areas such as layout generation, color schemes, and interactive element design. Results indicate that UI-GAN can rapidly generate diverse design schemes, with layout module counts ranging from 5 to 8 on different devices, color scheme generation times between 1.8 and 2.3 seconds, and interactive element response times of 100 to 180 milliseconds. This significantly improves design efficiency and optimizes user experience.

title: Inserting Generative Learning Activities During Pauses in Slideshow and Virtual Reality Lessons
venue: Journal of Computer Assisted Learning
abstract: Background: Generative learning activities, such as self-explanation, have been shown to enhance learning outcomes. However, it remains unclear whether their benefits persist across different types of media with various levels of distraction. Objectives: This study addressed three questions: (1) a value-added question, (2) a media comparison question and (3) an individual differences question. Method: On day one of the experiment, participants learned about ocean acidification in one of four randomly assigned conditions: immersive virtual reality (IVR) lesson with self-explanation prompts (IVR+), IVR lesson without prompts (IVR), a slideshow lesson with self-explanation prompts (slideshow+) or a slideshow lesson without prompts. Participants in the self-explanation conditions were prompted to explain the previous segment during each of four pauses in the lesson. One week later, participants completed a delayed posttest as well as several executive function tasks. Results and Conclusion: Results demonstrated that participants who received self-explanation prompts scored significantly higher on the posttest than those who did not, supporting the value-added question hypothesis. Additionally, executive function scores significantly correlated with posttest scores for participants who learned in IVR, but not for those in the slideshow conditions, supporting the individual differences question. However, there were no significant differences in learning outcomes between the IVR and slideshow conditions, countering the media comparison hypothesis. The importance of these findings is discussed. © 2026 John Wiley & Sons Ltd.

title: InsightAR: A Tool for Multi-modal Summarization and Interactive Analysis of AR-based Egocentric Task Videos
venue: Proceedings of the 2026 International Conference on Advanced Visual Interfaces, AVI 2026
abstract: The growing use of head-mounted AR devices has produced a surge of egocentric recordings of procedural tasks - step-by-step activities such as medical procedures - creating rich opportunities for performance analysis. Yet current analyses are time-consuming, requiring substantial manual inspection to identify events, actions, and objects from videos, with little automated support for surfacing insights or errors. We introduce InsightAR, a visual analytics tool that integrates event detection, action recognition, and multi-modal language models to create video summaries capturing key errors and insights. Its interface further enables users to refine generated insights and errors collaboratively. A user study (N=16) found that InsightAR identifies significantly more errors and marginally significant insight numbers than the baseline. Our work demonstrated the feasibility and potential benefits of future human-AI collaborative video analysis. © 2026 Copyright held by the owner/author(s).

title: Instruction Finetuning DeepSeek Based LLM Model for Financial Sentiment and Topic Classification
venue: Proceedings of the 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Interaction Design
abstract: Financial text classification benchmarking has been widely used in quantitative trading systems development, and typical tasks involve financial sentiment classification and classification of financial news. Here, we look to the more recent application of advanced natural language processing (NLP) techniques. This study looks at the performance of the DeepSeek model (a large language model with 7B parameters) on both tasks. As stock and futures markets continue to grow in complexity, quantitative trading systems can not only process price data of financial products, but must also react in real-time to news and investor sentiment.In this research, we finetuned the DeepSeek Model using Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) on a Twitter based financial news dataset and financial sentiment classification dataset. We also implemented FlashAttention to speed up training time and use less GPU memory. In our experiments, we compared DeepSeek's performance against those of traditional non-LLM models including RoBERTa, DeBERTa and T5 and also large language models such as LLaMA2 and Baichuan2. The results indicated that DeepSeek outperformed the traditional models and the LLMs even with fewer training iterations. The results showed the benefits of the DeepSeek approach, as it produced better classification results with less data and fewer training epochs, thus overall providing a solid basis for future ethical and widely scalable applications of NLP in the media space.

title: Integrating AI, VR, CAD, and Rapid Prototyping for Multi-Utility Electric Vehicle Cabin Design
venue: International Journal of Design and Nature and Ecodynamics
abstract: This study develops and validates an integrated digital workflow for multi-utility electric vehicle (EV) cabin design in an emerging-market manufacturing context. The workflow links AI-assisted concept exploration, SolidWorks Computer-Aided Design (CAD) modelling, Virtual Reality (VR) ergonomic evaluation, Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) simulation, and rapid prototyping in a continuous feedback loop from concept generation to physical validation. The cabin requirements differ from passenger EVs because the platform must support mixed cargo-passenger use, frequent ingress-egress, robust dashboard and door-panel packaging, driver visibility in urban logistics operations, and low-cost manufacturability. The study generated 12 AI-assisted styling variants, evaluated the cabin through VR with 5 representative participants covering the 95th anthropometric percentile range, and analyzed 1 CFD case at 80 km/h. CFD analysis produced a drag coefficient of approximately 0.404, within the expected 0.35-0.50 range for utility EV bodies. Physical validation used a 1:10 exterior prototype and 1:1 dashboard and door-panel mockups fabricated through 3D printing/manual finishing, with dimensional checks against CAD data. The workflow also supported an underfloor cargo innovation registered as IPR No. S00202511613 The findings show that early VR feedback reduces downstream ergonomic rework, CFD-guided refinement improves aerodynamic behavior, and rapid prototyping confirms manufacturability, offering a scalable model for EV design by small and medium manufacturers in Indonesia and similar emerging markets. ©2026 The authors.

title: Integrating Generative AI and GAN for Personalized Fashion and Clothing Design
venue: Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems
abstract: This research explores how AI can help to create fashion items that truly fits each person’s preference and style, body shape and way of living. Through AI technology fashion design experienced a change in which the system creates customized apparel that matches customer body measurements and fashion choices. AI establishes the ability to boost every stage of design development by integrating intelligent systems and creative functions beginning at conceptual design until final manufacturing. The use of GANs enables designers to see computer-generated clothes and three-dimensional models before physical production which shortens time and reduces waste and increases efficiency. AI completes three essential functions by foreseeing upcoming fashion trends as well as selecting adaptable fabrics according to weather patterns while designing items that merge style with comfort. Thus, fashion becomes easier to reach and less costly so a larger number of people can purchase custom-made fashionable clothes. AI serves the environment by eliminating production waste while producing clothing specifically when there is demand.AI technology establish a sustainable marketplace between producers and end-users by optimizing product development production. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.

title: Integrating Generative AI Assistant into Social VR Classroom for Medical Education: System Design and Implementation
venue: Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems
abstract: In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) has been increasingly integrated into educational settings. Traditional teaching methods often fail to explain complex anatomical structures in virtual environments where spatial visualization is critical. Despite offering familiar advantages, conventional teaching approaches do not offer educators real-time, adaptive support for interactive 3D content. To address these challenges, this study examines the application of generative AI tutor assistants in virtual reality classrooms. This assistant is specifically designed to support educators in teaching 3D cardiac visualization to students, which serves as a case study in this research. Initial expert evaluation (n=10) showed the AI tutor outperformed traditional methods across all measured dimensions including Realism Enhancement and Adaptive Learning abilities. The next phase of this research involves a comprehensive evaluation of the prototype with students and teachers, examining the AI tutor's ability to teach effectively, provide accurate content, and adapt to different learning needs of students. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.

title: Integrating Generative AI with VR and AR: Enhancing Immersive Educational Experiences Via Authentic Learning and Assessment
venue: Generative AI in Education: Theories, Applications, and Ethical Frontiers
abstract: The integration of Generative AI with Virtual and Augmented Reality technologies represents a significant shift in educational approaches, facilitating immersive learning experiences through personalized and adaptive environments for students. This chapter examines the interplay of these technologies in facilitating personalized learning, enhancing engagement and collaboration, and promoting critical thinking. Generative AI offers adaptive content customized to individual learner requirements, effectively integrating with the immersive characteristics of VR/AR to enhance comprehension and learner satisfaction. This concept is implemented via scenario-based adaptive simulations, allowing students to engage in life-like events consistent with Constructivist and Situated Learning Theories. Real-time feedback and dynamic content adjustment, aligned with the learner’s progress, will mitigate cognitive overload and improve focus, as supported by Cognitive Load Theory and the Theory of Flow. Generative AI, integrated into immersive technologies, enables authentic assessment of performance in complex, real-world tasks that support critical thinking and problem-solving skills. Instructional designers can strategically leverage the integration of such technologies to enrich learning experiences, address practical challenges, and lead effective implementations by drawing on frameworks like TPACK, SAMR, and Technology Acceptance Models. The ethical considerations in utilizing such technologies are equally significant, particularly regarding data privacy and equitable access. This synthesis of Generative AI and immersive learning technologies presents a future-oriented approach to education, integrating instructional design, learner engagement, and assessment to create a deeper, more accessible, and effective learning experience. © The Editor(s) (if applicable) and The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2026.

title: Integrating Generative Artificial Intelligence and Augmented Reality Within a Structured Project-Based Learning Framework for Unit Operations Education
venue: Sustainability (Switzerland)
abstract: This study examines the impact of integrating Generative Artificial Intelligence (AIgen) and Augmented Reality (AR) within a Project-Based Learning (PBL) framework to enhance student motivation and active learning in Chemical Engineering Unit Operations (OU) courses. The research employed a quasi-experimental post-test design without a control group and followed a mixed-methods explanatory approach. The intervention was implemented over two academic semesters at the Universidad Técnica Particular de Loja. The instructional design was structured using the 4PADAFE model, based on the principles of constructive alignment and competency-based education. The intervention was organized into seven sequential phases that integrated pedagogical planning, technological implementation, and evaluation. Students collaboratively developed educational resources, including interactive AR visualizations and AI-generated teaching materials addressing key topics such as fluid flow, heat transfer, and adsorption kinetics. The quantitative component constituted the main analytical approach and assessed changes in motivation using the Instructional Materials Motivation Survey (IMMS), based on Keller’s ARCS model. The instrument’s reliability was supported by high internal consistency (Cronbach’s α > 0.95) and satisfactory factor adequacy indices. The results revealed increases in all motivational dimensions, with mean scores rising from 3.26–3.33 in Phase I to 3.48–3.60 in Phase II. Overall, the findings indicate that the structured integration of AIgen and AR within an aligned problem-based learning (PBL) framework was associated with improvements in student engagement, confidence, and satisfaction. The study provides evaluative evidence supporting the implementation of technology-enhanced teaching strategies in engineering education under real-world classroom conditions. © 2026 by the authors.

title: Integrating Simulation-Based LLM Coaching for Adaptive Mixed-Reality Manufacturing Training
venue: Communications in Computer and Information Science
abstract: Operator training in advanced manufacturing demands precise and specific feedback that scales beyond what human experts can provide. We present a Mixed Reality (MR) training system for thermoforming that integrates Large Language Model (LLM)-generated coaching directly into the operator’s practice workflow. Building on a validated physics-based heat transfer simulation and spatial performance dashboard from prior work, this paper introduces an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based architecture that translates real-time simulation telemetry into structured, session-aware coaching delivered in-headset after each training run. Rather than generic feedback, each LLM coaching session is customized to the operator’s specific interaction patterns in each run and also is grounded in the process parameters such as zone-level temperature errors, energy consumption, and full prior-run history. This produces four labelled sections in the LLM coaching dashboard: Zone Analysis, Energy and Time, Trend, and an Overall Summary. A preliminary study with six novice operators found that all participants improved across four sequential training profiles, with group mean Zone Temperature Error reducing from 33.3 °C to 8.2 °C (a mean reduction of 74.9%). ‘LLM Coaching Specificity’ was the highest-rated category in the post study qualitative questionnaire (M = 6.42/7), where ‘Openness to AI’ and ‘Perceived Usefulness’ were also measured. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.

title: Integrating Terrestrial Laser Scanning, Generative AI, and Mixed Reality for Digital Heritage Reconstruction
venue: Journal of Visualized Experiments
abstract: The rapid acceleration of urbanization in developing regions has precipitated a dual crisis for architectural heritage: the physical degradation of structures and the intangible dissipation of cultural memory. Traditional conservation methodologies, which rely predominantly on static documentation, such as photography and manual surveying, are increasingly insufficient for capturing the complex spatial and temporal dimensions of these historic sites. This study introduces a novel, combinatorial methodological framework designed to bridge the gap between rigorous archiving and dynamic public engagement. We detail a workflow that synergizes three distinct technologies: Terrestrial Laser Scanning (TLS) to capture the tangible geometric attributes of the building with millimeter-level accuracy; Conditional Generative Artificial Intelligence (CGAI) to generate historically informed visual representations of lost cultural elements (specifically, traditional temple fair structures) based on archival references; and Augmented Reality (AR) via holographic headsets to superimpose these layers into a unified Mixed Reality (MR) experience. The protocol describes the complete pipeline from data acquisition strategies and point cloud processing to AI-driven model generation and final deployment. This approach yields a dynamic digital simulacrum that successfully overlays high-precision spatial data with interpretive cultural visualizations, offering a technically feasible and scalable workflow for the digital preservation and augmented exhibition of urban heritage landmarks. © 2026, Journal of Visualized Experiments.

title: Integrating Virtual Reality, Chatbots, and BDI Agents: VEsNA Goes Fast!
venue: Agents and Multi-Agent Systems Development: Platforms, Toolkits, Technologies
abstract: In the era of Generative Artificial Intelligence and the Metaverse, agents should be designed with social interaction involving humans in mind, and their situatedness should account for Virtual and eXtended Reality (VR/XR) environments. The social and the environmental contexts, where humans interact with agents in natural language and/or via virtual proxies in the form of avatars, should drive the agents’ decisions and actions. According to the strong definition, agents are conceptualized not only in terms of autonomy, situatedness, social interaction, proactivity, and reactivity but also through mentalistic attributes such as beliefs, desires, goals, and intentions. The Belief-Desire-Intention (BDI) model and architecture stick to the strong definition and are suitable to provide an explicit context to the agents’ reasoning and decision-making, which allow for explainability, transparency, and accountability. VEsNA has been conceived as the integration of the BDI architecture with chatbot-like interaction (possibly—although not necessarily—boosted by Generative AI, in particular Large Language Models) and situatedness in a Virtual Reality environment: VEsNA is an agent-based framework for managing Virtual Environments via Natural language Agents. title: Integrating VR and LLMs for Immersive Medical Training: Anaphylactic Shock Simulation
venue: Proceedings - European Council for Modelling and Simulation, ECMS
abstract: The integration of large language models (LLMs) into virtual reality (VR) medical simulation offers a promising direction for healthcare education, yet real-time responsiveness and medical accuracy remain critical challenges. This paper proposes an architecture for an LLM-powered virtual assistant in an anaphylactic shock VR training scenario, combining various optimization methods. The existing system is evaluated through a controlled experiment with nursing, medical, and midwifery students, who complete both a scripted and an AI-driven version of an anaphylaxis scenario. Biometric data, including EEG, ECG, and PPG biometric signals alongside questionnaires, are collected to assess immersion, stress response, and learning experience. Across the evaluated IPQ scales, scores were closely matched suggesting that the AI-driven simulation maintained a comparable level of presence to the scripted version. © ECMS Filippo Sanfilippo, Florenc Demrozi, Fabio Sgarbossa, Mohammad Poursina (Editors) 2026.

title: Intelligent Algorithm-Driven XR Film Content Production and User Precision Reach Mechanism
venue: 2026 3rd International Conference on Integrated Intelligence and Communication Systems (ICIICS)
abstract: History: Background Extended Reality (XR) films are a new paradigm in immersive storytelling that combines Virtual Reality, Augmented Reality and Mixed Reality technologies, but experiences widespread issues in production inefficiency and poor audience targeting. The existing production processes involve a lot of manual efforts and do not utilize computational intelligence to optimize them. Approaches: This work suggests a smart system that will utilize Generative Adversarial Networks, Reinforcement Learning and Deep Neural networks as a three-layer model that consists of content generation, optimization of production, and matching with users. The framework fully integrates script parsing based on LSTM, automated optimization of 3D asset generation, resource scheduling using genetic algorithm and multi-modal collaborative filtering to optimize the entire workflow. Findings: Experimental validation using 500 samples of 500 XR film proves the ability to reduce the production time by 67 percent, increase the quality measures of content by 43 percent and predict user preference by 82 percent, which is much better than the conventional methods. The practical applications of the system are confirmed in the real-time personalized recommendations, latency of 45ms and user satisfaction rate of 89%. Final Thoughts: The suggested algorithmic intervention is effective in increasing the efficiency of creativity and increasing the possibility of reaching the audience of the XR film ecosystem without sacrificing the quality requirements. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Intelligent Art Creation and Image Generation Method Based on Generative Adversarial Networks
venue: Proceedings of the 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Interaction Design
abstract: This paper addresses the challenges of insufficient style consistency and low detail fidelity in artistic style image generation. We propose an intelligent art creation method based on a deep convolutional generative adversarial network (DCGAN). Building on the traditional GAN framework, our method incorporates multi-layer convolutional feature fusion and style optimization modules to enhance the generated images' ability to capture the target artist's style. We construct a comprehensive technical system consisting of data preprocessing, feature extraction, generative model training, and style optimization, and conduct experimental validation on image data from a variety of artists' works. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing mainstream approaches on Inception Score (IS), Frechet Inception Distance (FID), and Structural Similarity (SSIM). FID is reduced by 12.7% and SSIM is improved by 8.4%, demonstrating significant advantages in detail representation and style restoration. This research not only improves the applicability of generative models in artistic creation but also provides a new technical path for intelligent and personalized art generation.

title: Intelligent Immersive Environments for Elderly Care: Integrating XR, Robotics, and AI Technologies
venue: Springer Proceedings in Business and Economics
abstract: This paper proposes the concept of an Intelligent Immersive Environment (IIE), an innovative eldercare framework integrating Extended Reality (XR), robotics, and Artificial Intelligence (AI). The proposed IIE aims to address critical eldercare challenges such as mobility impairments, cognitive decline, and social isolation by providing adaptive, personalized care solutions. XR technologies are envisioned to deliver immersive therapeutic sessions and cognitive training, robotics to offer physical support and companionship, and AI, including Generative AI and Large Language Models (LLMs), to dynamically personalize interactions based on user performance and emotional states. Emphasizing accessibility and inclusion, multimodal interfaces (voice, gesture, eye tracking) are proposed to accommodate diverse user needs. The framework outlines potential deployment pathways in residential care, assisted living facilities, and private homes, aiming to enhance quality of life, reduce caregiver burdens, and foster independence among elderly populations through holistic, technology-driven care solutions. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.

title: Intelligent Virtual Sonographer (IVS): Enhancing Physician-Robot-Patient Communication
venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science
abstract: The advancement and maturity of large language models (LLMs) and robotics have unlocked vast potential for human-computer interaction, particularly in the field of robotic ultrasound. While existing research primarily focuses on either patient-robot or physician-robot interaction, the role of an intelligent virtual sonographer (IVS) bridging physician-robot-patient communication remains underexplored. This work introduces a conversational virtual agent in Extended Reality (XR) that facilitates real-time interaction between physicians, a robotic ultrasound system(RUS), and patients. The IVS agent communicates with physicians in a professional manner while offering empathetic explanations and reassurance to patients. Furthermore, it actively controls the RUS by executing physician commands and transparently relays these actions to the patient. By integrating LLM-powered dialogue with speech-to-text, text-to-speech, and robotic control, our system enhances the efficiency, clarity, and accessibility of robotic ultrasound acquisition. This work constitutes a first step toward understanding how IVS can bridge communication gaps in physician-robot-patient interaction, providing more control and therefore trust into physician-robot interaction while improving patient experience and acceptance of robotic ultrasound. The code is available at https://github.com/stytim/IVS. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.

title: Interaction-Aware Shared Scene Synthesis for VR Telepresence
venue: IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics
abstract: Virtual reality telepresence requires immersive shared virtual environments for real-time remote collaboration across different physical scenes. It supports a wide range of applications in teleconferencing, education, and interactive simulations. However, challenges persist in identifying optimal shared virtual spaces that accommodate diverse user interaction requirements while adhering to local physical constraints during scene synthesis. In this paper, we propose an interaction-aware shared virtual scene synthesis method, which uses the large language model (LLM) to produce collaborative virtual scenes based on interaction demands from remote users in different local spaces. First, we introduce the concept of Interaction Aware Template (IAT) and its construction method using an LLM planner. Then, we propose an IAT-based affordance field alignment method for merging the local spaces of the remote users, maximally ensuring that the aligned space could support the user's desired interaction. Finally, we propose an LLM-based shared scene synthesis method according to the merged affordance field. Experiment results show that, compared to existing text-based scene synthesis and mutual space matching methods, our method achieves better Affordance Consistency, 3D Intersection over Union, and Layout Suitability on both scanned and synthesized datasets. The results of the user study demonstrate that the user's subjective perception of interaction fitness and sense of safety were significantly improved. © 1995-2012 IEEE.

title: Interactive Art Generation Model Optimization and Adaptive Adjustment Based on PPO Algorithm
venue: Proceedings of the 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Interaction Design
abstract: To address the persistent misalignment between individual aesthetic preferences and semantic intent in interactive art creation, this paper proposes a preference-feedback–driven optimization paradigm designed to balance generation quality, diversity, and stability under constrained latency. Methodologically, we construct a closed-loop framework—“preference acquisition → reward composition → proximal policy optimization → adaptive scheduling → controllable generation.” The framework fuses multi-source indicators with user preferences, employs PPO for stable policy updates, and leverages adaptive weighting with KL scheduling to curb distributional drift and reconcile multiple objectives. Experiments conducted on a unified backbone and evaluation protocol compare the proposed approach against an unaligned baseline, an aesthetics-guided post-processing method, and PPO without adaptivity. Results show consistent gains in semantic alignment and aesthetic scores (e.g., CLIP from 0.318 to 0.334; Aesthetic from 6.58 to 6.92), a substantial reduction in FID (29.7 to 26.8), and near-constant end-to-end latency; pairwise user studies also exhibit statistically significant win rates over all baselines. The contributions are threefold: (1) a reusable PPO-based adaptive alignment framework that integrates preference learning with generative control; (2) a stable training and evaluation protocol tailored to interactive settings; and (3) joint optimization of semantic alignment, aesthetic quality, diversity, and stability without incurring notable latency, offering a methodological foundation for practical deployment of personalized art generation systems.

title: Interactive Experiences in Extended Reality and Multimedia Environments
venue: IMX 2026 - Proceedings of the 2026 ACM International Conference on Interactive Media Experiences
abstract: This paper presents the research efforts of a doctoral program aimed at enabling enhanced, more natural and effective interactive experiences within immersive multimedia environments. The research builds on the development of an immersive virtual reconstruction of a demolished 16th-century theater, which serves as a comprehensive research framework to build upon. The work is structured around three main connected pillars: the multimodal reconstruction of historical heritage, the evaluation of interaction mechanics including shared multiuser visits, and the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) to exploit its potential within immersive media. Along this path, a controlled study comparing input and presentation methods for Virtual Reality (VR) user interfaces has been conducted, producing findings on the trade-offs between interaction methods and presence. Building on this work, planned directions include expanding the application with holoportation technologies, conducting further user evaluations, and investigating how generative AI could be applied within immersive media. This paper describes the completed work, the ongoing activities, and the planned directions. © 2026 Copyright held by the owner/author(s).

title: Interactive learning in digital art: the role of AI and collaborative platforms in shaping artistic expression
venue: Interactive Learning Environments
abstract: This study investigates how Interactive Learning Environments (ILEs) that integrate advanced software tools, collaborative digital platforms, immersive technologies, and AI support learning processes within digital art education contexts. This study investigated the impact of technology on boundaries of possible artistic expression in digital art through a mixed-methods study of 575 survey respondents–comprising 320 digital artists as learners and 255 art technicians, and 47 follow-on interviews that gathered rich qualitative data. Quantitative data were analyzed using Smart-PLS, and qualitative data were analyzed using Nvivo. The study demonstrates that (1) Advanced Software Tools Created an Enhanced Creative Workflow, (2) Collaborative Digital Platforms Enhanced a Range of Artistic Expression, (3) AR Provided a Seemingly Expansive Spatial and Immersive Experience in Digital Installations, and (4) AI allowed for Generative Creativity, creativity that extends or transports imagined forms of art and creativity via non-traditional arts and science based methods. These findings underpin the potential for a transformative digital art world using technology as a creative agent. This study deepens the growing field of human–technology interaction in creative domains, and sets up many research opportunities for the future of digital participation, collaboration, and immersion, and AI-enabled creative applications. © 2026 The Author(s). title: Interactive Virtual-Physical safety training for manufacturing workshops via vision and LLMs
venue: Digital Engineering
abstract: Effective operational training for production equipment is crucial to ensure personnel safety and realize the human-centric vision of Industry 5.0. However, existing Mixed Reality (MR)-based training methods in manufacturing workshops face two major challenges: difficulty in the semantic perception of equipment and lack of context-aware knowledge responses. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an interactive virtual-physical safety training for manufacturing workshops via vision and Large Language Models (LLMs). First, a methodological framework is established. Next, a machine vision-based semantic segmentation method combined with Vuforia multi-target recognition is employed to enable semantic understanding and 3D virtual-physical mapping of training equipment. Subsequently, a knowledge-grounded question answering method is introduced by integrating knowledge graphs and LLMs to support context-aware training feedback. Finally, a prototype safety training system is developed on HoloLens 2 and experimentally validated. Results show that, compared with traditional paper-based training, the proposed method shows potential to improve trainees’ performance in short-term tasks, particularly in skill-based training tasks under the present experimental conditions. These findings demonstrate its potential as a technical enabler for human-centered industrial safety training for workshop operators. © 2026

title: INTERVISION: An Intelligent Virtual Interview Simulator
venue: Proceedings of the 2026 International Conference on AI-Driven Smart Systems and Ubiquitous Computing, ICAUC 2026
abstract: This paper presents an AI-driven immersive virtual reality (VR) learning framework that integrates agentic artificial intelligence, speech based interaction, and real-time multiplayer collaboration. The proposed system utilizes the Gemini large language model to generate adaptive questions and feedback within the VR environment. Gemini is employed through structured prompt engineering and contextual memory mechanisms rather than parameter-level fine-tuning, enabling domain adaptation without modifying model weights. A user study involving 25 participants was conducted to assess interaction flow, system responsibilities, and overall user experience. Multiplayer performance evaluation using Photon PUN indicated stable synchronization across concurrent sessions, with observed network delays remaining within acceptable bounds for real time interaction, as shown in Figure 3.2. Speech recognition errors, such as mispronunciations and partial utterances, were found to momentarily affect question flow. However, system-level recovery prompts and confidence based feedback mechanisms helped maintain feedback consistency. The core contributions of this work include the integration of AI orchestration within a VR learning environment, real time speech driven interaction, and an empirical multiplayer system analysis. Limitations of the study include a limited participant pool, reliance on cloud based AI services and sensitivity to network conditions © 2026 IEEE.

title: Introduction to Generative Artificial Intelligence
venue: Generative Artificial Intelligence for Next-Generation Security Paradigms
abstract: “Generative AI” is a subpart of artificial intelligence that creates new content similar to the data it was trained on instead of just interpreting and evaluating pre-existing information. Unlike the outmoded Artificial Intelligence systems that are designed for specific tasks, Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) system models can produce novel products across various areas or domains, such as images, text, music, and more. At the core of generative AI are generative models, which learn the underlying patterns and structures of the training data and then use that knowledge to generate new samples. GAI has several applications across different types of domains, such as image generation, Video cohort and NLP etc. Many models have been implicated in applications like the entertainment industry, virtual reality, and generative models like Open AI’s GPT (Generative Pre-Trained Transformer) series can generate intelligible and contextually relevant text based on the provided input. Such models have applications in content generation, dialogue systems, and language translation. However, GAI also raises moral concerns; generated materials are prospectively misused. Example, images which are fake and streaming videos created by Artificial Intelligence could be used for dishonest purposes, leading to manipulation and misinformation of data. Researchers and policymakers are actively working to address these concerns by developing detection techniques and promoting responsible use of generative technology. ChatGPT uses to ascertain the most suitable answer for a particular command, hence enhancing the accuracy and dependability of the model over time. With this method, ChatGPT can comprehend human preferences in lengthy conversations more effectively. Chatbots by generative AI can work round the clock with uninterrupted services. Generative AI behaves like augmented human agents. Despite of series of hypes surrounding artificial intelligence, even the attackers appear to agree that ChatGPT’s release represents a sea change. With the help of its most recent broad language model, Open AI’s Chatbot can compose essays, poetry, and jokes that seem to have been written by a person. Say a few expressions to prompt ChatGPT, and love poems in the style of Yelp reviews or Nick Cave-inspired song lyrics emerge. It encompasses several techniques, including generative adversarial networks (GANs), vibrational auto encoders (VAEs), and autoregressive models. © 2026 Scrivener Publishing LLC.

title: Inverse Theory of Mind Modeling for Content Recommendation: From Web Browsing to Dynamic Intelligent Interfaces
venue: Proceedings of the 20th ACM Conference on Recommender Systems
abstract: Modern recommender systems treat observed actions as reliable proxies for user preferences, yet interactions often reflect exploration or comparison rather than stable preference expression. As interfaces evolve from static layouts toward generative UIs and immersive extended reality (XR), the need for deeper, modality-agnostic user understanding grows: these adaptive environments must decide not only what to present but where, when, how prominently, and most importantly why a user acts. We propose an Inverse Theory of Mind (IToM) pipeline that reasons backward from observed interactions to infer the beliefs, preferences, and decision-making traits that explain behavior. The pipeline reconstructs each user’s decision context, including what was chosen and what alternatives were available, applies LLM-driven counterfactual reasoning to produce evidence-grounded natural-language belief statements, and synthesizes these beliefs through multi-hypothesis abductive inference into a structured user persona. We evaluate on the OPeRA dataset against ground-truth personality assessments, attitudinal surveys, and interview-based personas across four tasks: next action prediction, shopping attitude alignment, Big Five personality inference, and held-out category prediction. Results show that inferred personas match or exceed ground-truth personas and that multi-hypothesis reasoning is essential for accurate personality prediction. We further demonstrate cross-modal transferability with a persona-driven spatial banking application on VisionOS.

title: Investigating Designer Interaction with AI Text-to-Image Systems in Vision Pro for Transportation Design
venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science
abstract: Recent advancements in generative AI and spatial computing offer transformative potential for integrating AI-assisted generation into early-stage design. However, the usability of text-to-image systems within immersive environments—offering true scale and spatial depth—remains underexplored for large-scale transportation design. This study investigates design behaviors and workflow implications of AI-driven image generation on Apple Vision Pro, focusing on biomimetic vehicle design. We conducted a quasi-experimental study with six participants (two experts and four novices) who performed shark- and eagle-inspired motorcycle design tasks in VR. Leveraging the Vision Pro’s high-resolution spatial display and head-tracking, participants iteratively refined designs using voice prompts and freehand sketching. Data from observations and semi-structured interviews were qualitatively analyzed to identify interaction patterns and designer-AI intent mismatches. Results indicate that while immersive VR significantly enhances scale perception and proportion assessment, current input modalities (voice and sketch) lack the precision of traditional desktop workflows. These findings suggest that future immersive design tools must bridge the gap between spatial visualization advantages and the need for high-precision input hardware. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.

title: Investigating Generative Workflows for Immersive Prototyping: A Study on Scene- and Object-Level Creation in VR
venue: Proceedings - 2026 IEEE Conference on Virtual Reality and 3D User Interfaces, VR 2026
abstract: The integration of generative AI into immersive prototyping tools offers unprecedented potential to accelerate VR content creation. However, a critical gap exists in understanding the most effective interaction paradigms. We present DreamCraft, a novel VR prototyping system designed to integrate two fundamental workflows: scene-level creation, where users generate entire, navigable environments, and object-level creation, where scenes are iteratively populated with AI-generated assets. A formal user study with 12 VR designers was conducted to evaluate these workflows, evaluating both workflows through qualitative feedback and quantitative metrics, including task completion time, creative exploration, and perceived cognitive load. Our primary contribution is a set of empirically-grounded design guidelines derived from this analysis. These guidelines provide a crucial framework for the development of next-generation, user-centric generative tools for immersive virtual environments, directly informing future research and system design in the field. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Investigating Player Perception of Environment-Aware Embodied Conversational Agents Enabled by Vision Language Models
venue: 2026 IEEE 5th International Conference on Intelligent Reality (ICIR)
abstract: Recent advancements in generative AI have enabled the integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) into Virtual Environments (VEs). This integration has been particularly useful to create Embodied Conversational Agents (ECAs) capable of engaging in meaningful interactions. However, such ECAs often lack environmental awareness, which may limit the quality of interactions and conversations. A potential solution could be to use Vision Language Models (VLMs), which could empower ECAs with structured environmental knowledge. However, the use of VLMs for such applications is largely underexplored. This paper explores how VLMs can be employed to integrate environmental awareness in ECAs and investigates their impact on player perception. To this end, an architecture leveraging multi-image inference and scene graph generation was designed. A within-subject user study was then conducted in a virtual reality game, comparing ECAs with and without environment-aware capabilities. The evaluation considered several dimensions, including perceived knowledge, intelligence, factuality, willingness of future interaction and conversational abilities. © 2026 IEEE.
