title: Processed Experience: A Contemporary Discourse on Existence with Spatial Installation
venue: ARTECH 2025 - 12th International Conference on Digital and Interactive Arts: Media Art Cultures, Communities and Territories
abstract: Now, we see proliferation of information and things of experience. We undergo numerous digital experiences, yet overwhelmed by their splendor and quantity, we struggle to articulate what we have experienced. This excess of experience dilutes the density of condensed experience and punctures our sense of being. This demands philosophical reflection. In response, this paper proposes “Processed Experience” as a conceptual framework for understanding how digital experiences are constructed through discontinuous, fragmented units rather than continuous flows. Drawing from information theory and media aesthetics, we introduce three analytical axes: Medium (material conditions of information), Frame (quantum segmentation of time), and Attention (selective information capture mechanisms). These three dimensions project experience into discrete units we call “Dice”, which are formed through Encoding and Processing within information field. To reveal the framework as phenomenon, we present a spatial installation using Apple Vision Pro. Participants are surrounded by three-dimensional graphics and audio manifested by different processor—RGB differentials, AI interpretations, and interpolated graphics. The installation places the outputs of different processors (electrical circuits, algorithms, language models) in front of another processor—the human participant. The three-minute immersive experience progressively overwhelms participant, forcing them to confront their own processing. By confronting participants within others’ processed outputs, it prompts questions about how digital experiences are constructed through encoding and processing. This research presents “Processthetics”—an aesthetic attitude where processing is experience itself. Rather than being confused by excess, understanding experience in novel framework opens new interpretive possibilities for digital experience and existence in the contemporary era. © 2025 Copyright held by the owner/author(s).

title: Product evaluation system design combining multimodal cross-attention mechanism and virtual reality technology-A case study of cockpit interior design
venue: Advanced Engineering Informatics
abstract: With the widespread application of Artificial Intelligence Generated Content (AIGC) in product design, designers can rapidly generate a large number of creative design proposals through keywords (Prompts). However, these massive outputs present a major challenge for product development. Designers struggle to efficiently identify concepts that truly align with enterprise needs from such a large volume of proposals. Therefore, this study proposes a dual-channel design evaluation system that integrates a multimodal cross-attention (MMCA) mechanism and virtual reality (VR) technology, using an automobile cockpit interior (CI) evaluation system as a case study. First, emotion evaluation indicators are constructed based on user affective vocabulary. Their corresponding weights are then calculated using the forward projection area (FPA) method. The MMCA model is then trained to map user emotions to CI design features, enabling the prediction of emotion scores for batches of input images and form codes. A diffusion model (DM) is subsequently employed to generate novel design samples based on large-scale learning from existing CI images, and the MMCA model is used to select preliminary schemes with high emotion scores. Finally, VR technology provides a 360° immersive experience to evaluate these preliminary schemes and determine the final design. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed system can rapidly identify optimal concepts from large volumes of AI-generated designs, reduce designers’ subjective bias and significantly improve the efficiency of moving from concept to realization. Moreover, the framework can be extended to the evaluation of other industrial product designs. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

title: Product Packaging Design Automation Optimization Based on Image Processing and GAN
venue: Proceedings of the 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Interaction Design
abstract: With the rapid development of artificial intelligence in the field of visual creativity, product packaging design is embracing new opportunities for automation and intelligence. However, traditional image generation methods still struggle to meet the complex aesthetic demands, layout structures, and printing compliance requirements of packaging design, often resulting in unstable generation quality and insufficient structural control. This paper proposes an optimization framework for packaging design that integrates image processing techniques with Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs). The framework incorporates structural preservation modules, semantic guidance mechanisms, and color printability constraints to enhance both visual appeal and industrial applicability. A multi-dimensional evaluation metric system was established, and extensive experiments were conducted on typical packaging scenarios such as beverages, personal care, and snacks. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms mainstream models in terms of aesthetic scores, OCR recognition accuracy, layout consistency, and color compliance. Notably, the model achieved superior performance in ΔE₀₀ color difference control and TAC violation rate. This study not only improves the visual and practical quality of generated designs but also provides a feasible technical path for intelligent packaging design generation.

title: Project SmartAvatar: A Human-Avatar Interface
venue: IMX 2026 - Proceedings of the 2026 ACM International Conference on Interactive Media Experiences
abstract: This paper presents SmartAgent, a real-time multimodal framework that integrates Large Language Models (LLMs), speech processing, and embodied avatar rendering to enable more natural and expressive human-computer interaction. The system introduces an embodied conversational agent, Bitzy, capable of interpreting user input and responding through synchronized speech, facial expressions, gestures, and gaze. To ensure consistency across modalities, a structured JSON schema is used to bridge cognitive processing and real-time animation in Unity. The architecture adopts a modular design that decouples speech recognition, language generation, and rendering, improving scalability and responsiveness. Preliminary results indicate that the proposed approach enhances user engagement, perceived presence, and interaction quality when compared to traditional text-based interfaces. These findings suggest that multimodal embodied agents represent a promising direction for developing more human-centered interactive systems. © 2026 Copyright held by the owner/author(s).

title: Projection-Based Augmented Reality for Lean Drone Assembly: Reducing Waste and Enhancing Learning Efficiency
venue: Procedia Computer Science
abstract: This study explores the integration of Augmented Reality (AR) into Lean Manufacturing practices to enhance manual drone assembly training. Leveraging lean principles such as Jidoka, standardized work, and visual management, a projection-based AR system was developed featuring real-time task guidance, gesture control, and voice interaction. A structured methodology: Set up, Testing and Evaluation, was used to compare the performance of AR-assisted and traditional non-AR training. Participants across both conditions completed identical tasks, with results revealing that AR users completed tasks 22.3% faster and committed no defects, compared to several errors in the control group. Furthermore, learning curve analysis showed a 4.1% greater improvement in skill acquisition among AR users. By embedding lean tools directly into the AR interface, the system reduced waste related to waiting, over-processing, and errors, while enabling scalable, hands-free instruction. Although Vision-Language Model (VLM) integration remains a future enhancement, the current implementation demonstrates AR's capacity to streamline training, improve consistency, and support workforce development within Industry 4.0-aligned environments. © 2026 The Author(s).

title: Prompt-to-Touch: Towards Enabling Automatic Haptic Effect Generation from Text Prompts Using Text-to-Audio Models
venue: ACM Transactions on Computer-Human Interaction
abstract: We introduce Prompt-to-Touch, a proof-of-concept of a multi-step pipeline that generates haptic effects based on the textual description of a haptic experience. Our pipeline first translates the haptic effect description to a sound effect description using our Foley-Interpreter component. It then uses a text-to-audio model to generate a sound effect from the sound description. Afterwards, the sound effect is converted into a perceivable haptic effect using our Dynamic-Audio-Processor. Finally, the haptic effect is post-processed to compensate for actuator-specific frequency response characteristics. We validate our concept in two preliminary human evaluation studies (n = 20, n = 10) and a technical analysis. Our results indicate that our pipeline can generate effects to enhance immersive multimedia experiences, abstract desktop/XR interactions, and social communication applications. They also still reveal significant potential for further improvement. Our pipeline could be used to develop future text-driven haptic design and automation tools. We provide open-source code to support future extensions. © 2026 Copyright held by the owner/author(s).

title: Prompting for Mindfulness: User-Generated AI Environments for Multisensory Box Breathing in Virtual Reality
venue: IH 2026 - Proceedings of the 2026 ACM Interactive Health Conference
abstract: Prompting for Mindfulness is a virtual reality prototype that explores how user-prompted generative AI can be used to create a personalized, multi-sensory environment for mindful guided breathing. Its application context is as a tool to relieve symptoms of emotional-coping related digital platform overuse. Through a spoken natural language prompt, users describe their ideal relaxation space which is translated into a skybox and soundscape using AI. Users' attention is then directed to their internal bodily sensations by tactile cardio-feedback of their heart rate, followed by guided box breathing via synchronized visual and haptic cues, finishing with cardio feedback again. By immersing users in an engaging environment that they have co-created, the user is motivated to direct all attentional focus towards the present moment and body sensations through visual, auditory, and tactile engagement. The prototype aims to facilitate a meaningful connection to the environment itself via the personalization element to increase engagement with the overall experience. © 2026 Copyright held by the owner/author(s).

title: Prop-Chromeleon: Adaptive Haptic Props in Mixed Reality through Generative Artificial Intelligence
venue: DIS 2026 - Proceedngs of the 2026 ACM Designing Interactive Systems Conference
abstract: Mixed Reality (MR) aims to blend digital and physical worlds, but the absence of haptic feedback often breaks visual-tactile consistency. We introduce Prop-Chromeleon, a MR system based on generative artificial intelligence (AI) that dynamically transforms everyday objects into adaptive passive haptic props through user-provided text prompts. Our AI pipeline performs generation and anchoring of virtual assets that align with the shape of physical props, allowing us to study how virtual content generation behaves under geometric and prompt-based constraints. We evaluate Prop-Chromeleon's effectiveness through a generation study using varied object shapes and user prompts, combining quantitative shape similarity metrics with qualitative prompt fidelity analysis. Our user study further showcases Prop-Chromeleon's improvements in perceived realism, immersion, and enjoyment compared to static baselines. These results show that shape-aware generation can support both believable haptic interaction and creative engagement in MR. © 2026 Copyright held by the owner/author(s).

title: Prototyping an LLM-Based AI Agent for Operator Support in Augmented Reality Industrial Quality Inspection
venue: Proceedings - 2026 10th International Young Engineers Forum on Electrical and Computer Engineering, YEF-ECE 2026
abstract: This paper presents the design, implementation, and initial empirical evaluation of an LLM-based AI agent integrated into an Augmented Reality (AR) environment for quality inspection support in an Industry 5.0 manufacturing context. The fully implemented system combines spatially anchored visual overlays with a conversational AI assistant grounded in a deployed Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline over Manuel da Conceição Graça, Lda official inspection documentation. A preliminary within-subject user study (N= 6) was conducted to compare two implemented input modalities, virtual keyboard and speech-to-text, across a set of simulated industrial inspection tasks. The objective of the study was to assess the usability of the implemented system with first-time AR users, and to determine which input modality better fits the hands-busy demands of shop-floor inspection. Results show that voice interaction was consistently preferred for ease of use, speed, and comfort, while the virtual keyboard was perceived as more precise but more demanding. Both conditions received positive SUS scores, confirming that the implemented system is usable without domainspecific training. © 2026 IEEE.

title: ProXeek: Seeking and Leveraging Real-World Objects and Environments as Haptic Proxies for Virtual Reality through Multimodal Reasoning
venue: ACM Transactions on Graphics
abstract: Providing haptic feedback in virtual reality (VR) remains challenging, with active haptic systems often being bulky and expensive, while passive haptics typically require pre-fabricated objects or extensive real-world setup. We present ProXeek, an LLM-based multi-agent system that opportunistically leverages real-world objects as haptic proxies for VR experiences. During VR development, the designers could annotate the virtual interactables with emphasized haptic characteristics using our node-based editing interface. On the user side, end users capture environmental snapshots via commodity VR headset, and the system employs LLM-based multimodal reasoning and multi-objective optimization to match virtual objects with viable physical proxies. Our technical evaluation demonstrates that ProXeek effectively identifies viable proxies, confirming the effectiveness of the algorithmic constraint design in our matching pipeline. Our user study further reveals that the ProXeek-selected physical objects could deliver significantly higher haptic fidelity and enhance presence compared to 3D-printed replicas and visual-only interaction. © 2026 Copyright held by the owner/author(s).

title: PVSDNet: Joint Depth Prediction and View Synthesis Via Shared Latent Spaces in Real-Time
venue: IEEE Access
abstract: Recent advances in real-time view synthesis have significantly enhanced immersive augmented telepresence applications by providing new viewpoints. Accurate depth estimation enables precise placement of virtual objects and improves spatial understanding and interaction. Nevertheless, state-of-the-art monocular depth estimation methods, when applied independently to each synthesized view, often result in geometric inconsistencies and visual artifacts such as flickering. To address these limitations, we propose a unified multimodal network capable of jointly synthesizing new views and predicting consistent depth maps from a single input image. Our framework integrates an additional depth prediction module into a state-of-the-art view synthesis architecture by leveraging a shared latent representation, thereby ensuring geometric coherence between synthesized views and their depth maps. We introduce a two-stage training strategy, initially freezing the view synthesis branch of the network while training the depth decoder individually to establish accurate depth estimation. Subsequently, we fine-tune the combined architecture employing low-rank adaptation (LoRA), facilitating rapid convergence and improved multimodal accuracy. Extensive experiments validate that our proposed approach achieves superior viewpoint consistency, visual realism, and depth accuracy while maintaining real-time inference speeds, highlighting its suitability for live interactive augmented telepresence environments.

title: Qualitative Study of 3D Object Generation in Immersive Technologies
venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science
abstract: 3D generative content (3DGC) is considered an intersection between Artificial Intelligence Generated Content (AIGC) and Extended Reality (XR). AIGC tools, initially popular for text and image generation, have expanded to audio, video, and 3D objects. Among the numerous 3D object generative methods, we explore in this work some 3D object generative models from a single image (2D-to-3D), due to their potential for immersive applications. This article aims to investigate, using qualitative methods, users’ perceptions of 3DGC in an XR environment through a head mounted display (HMD). In this study, we obtained deep insights related to the dimensions that would be overall 3D object quality, image-to-object correspondence, and user satisfaction regarding generation time, involving 40 participants. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.

title: Quantifying Latencies: A Conversation Analysis Approach to Human-Agent Interactions in Virtual Reality
venue: Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems - Proceedings
abstract: Users feel frustrated when they do not know when to speak with LLM-based agents. Technical delays disrupt the natural rhythm of conversation (turn-taking), yet there is little understanding of how these specific delays impact the back-and-forth flow of interaction. To address this, we analyzed human-agent conversations in social VR to measure timing differences. We used conversation analysis techniques to track specific timing metrics, such as how long it takes to respond (response latencies) and how agents handle interruptions (repair attempts). We found that agents are significantly slower to respond with a median of 4.1 seconds compared to a human's 1.2 seconds. We identified a "conversational timing drift", noting that agents struggle with start-up latency, i.e., taking too long to start speaking, and wind-down latency, i.e., failing to stop speaking quickly when a user interrupts them. This is the first study to empirically quantify human-agent conversational latencies within VR. We offer design suggestions to help future agents manage conversational timing better, ultimately improving natural conversation and user experience. © 2026 Copyright held by the owner/author(s).

title: Quantitative Evaluation and Domain Adaptation of Vision–Language Models for Mixed-Reality Interpretation of Indoor Environmental Computational Fluid Dynamics Visualizations
venue: Technologies
abstract: In built environmental design, incorporating building user participation and verifying indoor thermal performance at early design stages have become increasingly important. Although Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) analysis is widely used to predict indoor thermal environments, its results are difficult for non-expert stakeholders to interpret, even when visualized using Mixed Reality (MR). Interpreting CFD visualizations in MR requires quantitative reasoning that explicitly cross-references visual features with legend information, rather than relying on prior color–value associations learned from natural images. This study investigates the capability of Vision–Language Models (VLMs) to interpret MR visualizations of CFD results and respond to user queries. We focus on indoor temperature distributions and airflow velocities visualized in MR. A novel dataset was constructed, consisting of MR images with CFD results superimposed onto real indoor spaces, paired with domain-specific question–answer annotations requiring legend-based reasoning. Using this dataset, a general-purpose VLM (Qwen2.5-VL) was fine-tuned. Experimental results show that the baseline model achieved less than 30% accuracy, whereas fine-tuning improved accuracy to over 60% across all categories while largely preserving general reasoning performance. These results demonstrate that domain adaptation enables VLMs to quantitatively interpret physical information embedded in MR visualizations, supporting non-experts’ understanding of built environmental design. © 2026 by the authors.

title: Radiation Therapy Operation Training Prototype Systems Using 3D Models Generated by PartPacker
venue: Lecture Notes on Data Engineering and Communications Technologies
abstract: This paper treats the development of radiation therapy operation training systems. For the operation training systems of various types of radiation therapy equipment, their 3D models should be prepared. The authors investigated how easily create such 3D models using Generative AI tools, and performed 3D model generation experiments using several Generative AI tools. As a result, the authors developed radiation therapy operation training prototype systems using the 3D models actually generated by PartPacker, one of the Generative AI tools for 3D models. In this paper, the authors report the experimental results of 3D model generation and introduce how radiation therapy operation training prototype systems can be developed using the generated 3D models. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.

title: RaySound Vision: A Cloud-Edge Collaborative Multimodal AR Assistive System for the Elderly
venue: 2026 International Wireless Communications and Mobile Computing Conference, IWCMC 2026
abstract: With the accelerating trend of population aging, elderly individuals increasingly face age-related sensory degradation, particularly visual and auditory impairments, which significantly hinder their daily activities and medication safety. While traditional smartphone-based assistive applications offer basic age-friendly features, they often impose a "digital fence"characterized by high cognitive friction in interaction paradigms and a severe disconnect from real-time physical environments. To address these critical social pain points, we propose RaySound Vision, a multimodal smart sensory enhancement system deployed on RayNeo X2 augmented reality (AR) glasses. By transforming multi-step manual operations into intuitive, first-person natural interactions, we construct a wearable "sensory agent"that provides barrier-free assistance. Our main technical contributions are three-fold: 1) we design an end-to-cloud streaming architecture to handle intensive multimodal tasks; 2) we implement a customized YOLO and regional OCR pipeline optimized for robust medication identification in complex environments; and 3) we present a comprehensive empirical analysis of system latency across different processing stages (network, local perception, and LLM reasoning). Our real-world evaluations demonstrate that for complex medical reasoning, the system strategically prioritizes semantic fidelity and cognitive safety over raw processing speed, establishing a necessary latency-accuracy trade-off that effectively reconstructs a reliable and accessible sensory world for the elderly. © 2026 IEEE.

title: (Re)thinking Sexual and Reproductive Health Education with Bloom's Taxonomy
venue: DIS 2026 - Proceedngs of the 2026 ACM Designing Interactive Systems Conference
abstract: Sexual and Reproductive Health (SRH) education remains largely limited to awareness-based interventions, particularly in stigmatized socio-cultural contexts. Researchers are extensively focusing on pedagogical theories, reshaping teaching and learning practices to enhance educational outcomes. This paper investigates the application of Bloom's taxonomy as a design framework for scaffolding SRH learning from foundational knowledge to higher-order cognitive engagement. We conducted a mixed-methods study with 45 participants who engaged in learning activities across different cognitive levels, followed by semi-structured interviews. Our analysis shows that integrating higher-order learning objectives - such as application, analysis, and reflection - supports deeper engagement and understanding of SRH topics beyond surface-level awareness. We also highlight how technologies such as VR and LLMs enable flexible, exploratory learning and create safe, judgment-free spaces for engaging with sensitive topics, supporting users' comfort. Based on these findings, we derive design implications for developing structured, inclusive, and stigma-sensitive SRH education technologies. This work contributes to HCI by empirically demonstrating how established learning theories can advance learning in sensitive educational domains. © 2026 Copyright held by the owner/author(s).

title: Re:Vive: An Intelligent Interactive Platform for Cultural Discovery Through AI, NLP, and AR
venue: 2026 5th International Conference on Communication, Computing and Electronics Systems (ICCCES)
abstract: The rich cultural traditions and customs of India, the folklore, stories, and history of this country are, unfortunately, being simply at risk of becoming a dead end and are bound to vanish or lose their relevance in our technologically oriented digital world. The conventional digital heritage web sites tend to be lacking in the respective areas of interactivity, personalization, as well as the immersive experience, which can make the current audience interested, as important, the youth audience. This study presents Re: Vive: a smart experiment that combines Artificial Intelligence (AI), Natural Language Processing (NLP), and Augmented Reality into one (AR) to provide interactive and personalized experiences in cultural exploration. Re:Vive model focuses on the real-time user interactions and rewriting of the narrative, contrary to the episodic and network systems of other heritage systems. A backend of the system is scalable and, therefore, can be used in AIrecommendation, NLP-conversational storytelling, and ARvisualization.

title: Reading the Mood Behind Words: Integrating Prosody-Derived Emotional Context into Socially Responsive VR Agents
venue: Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems - Proceedings
abstract: In VR interactions with embodied conversational agents, users' emotional intent is often conveyed more by how something is said than by what is said. However, most VR agent pipelines rely on speech-to-text processing, discarding prosodic cues and often producing emotionally incongruent responses despite correct semantics. We propose an emotion-context-aware VR interaction pipeline that treats vocal emotion as explicit dialogue context in an LLM-based conversational agent. A real-time speech emotion recognition model infers users' emotional states from prosody, and the resulting emotion labels are injected into the agent's dialogue context to shape response tone and style. We conducted a within-subjects VR study (N = 30) using semantically neutral and emotionally ambiguous utterances, comparing an emotion-aware agent with a text-only baseline. Results show significant improvements in dialogue quality, naturalness, engagement, rapport, and human-likeness, with 93.3% of participants preferring the emotion-aware agent. These findings suggest that prosody-derived emotional context enables socially responsive VR conversations. © 2026 Copyright held by the owner/author(s).

title: Real-Time AI-Based Virtual Interview Panel with Multimodal Feedback and Adaptive Personality Simulation
venue: 2026 International Conference on Sustainable Engineering and Technology Innovations, ICSETI 2026
abstract: This paper reports on the launch of a real-time AI-assisted virtual interviewer panel that is intended to simulate human-like interviewer behaviour using multimodal analysis and psychological modeling. Current platforms commonly incorporate AI technology but do not demonstrate emotional intelligence and thus, lack the ability to demonstrate realism and better accuracy in assessment. This new model combines Natural Language Processing, Speech Analytics, Computer Vision, and Biofeedback Sensing to analyse both communication and signs of stress. The panel embraces Eysenck's Personality Theory with three basic types of AI interviewers - friendly, analytical, and strict -that modulate based on responses in each session adaptively. The employed Large Language Models (LLM) and Virtual Reality Exposure Therapy, enhance realism while providing the candidate, a familiar high-fidelity experience to assist with anxiety and develop confidence prior to job interviews. This research explores an example of how AI and psychology can create a more immersive and emotionally intelligent interview experience. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Real-Time Classroom Simulation with Generative AI: An Immersive Environment for Teacher Emotion-Regulation Training
venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science
abstract: Preparing teachers for emotionally charged classroom disruptions is still largely based on in-person roleplays, which are difficult to standardize and resource-intensive to facilitate. To address this gap, we developed an immersive VR training application that enables safe, repeatable practice with disruptive classroom scenarios. The system supports real-time spoken interaction with AI-driven student avatars and adapts dynamically to teacher interventions. At its core, a single generative model coordinates the full class as a coherent social simulation, while auxiliary modules manage disruption escalation and generate formative feedback on teacher responses. A pilot study with 15 participants showed high immersion and emotional engagement, supporting the feasibility of VR for emotion-regulation training. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.

title: Real-time edge intelligence using State-Gated Spectral VAD for multimodal streaming on resource-constrained devices
venue: International Journal of Electronics and Telecommunications
abstract: Multimodal AI streaming is used to enable real-time interaction in educational applications. It is a critical component in the integration of AI-driven Augmented Reality (AR) for language learning. The challenge faced in AI streaming is maintaining responsiveness on resource-constrained devices in regions with unstable network infrastructure. The previous algorithms which work well in high-bandwidth environments cannot be dominant at the network edge due to heavy resource consumption and latency spikes. This paper proposes an altered form of streaming architecture, termed State-Gated Spectral Voice Activity Detector (SG-SVAD), which produces a highly responsive, full-duplex multimodal interaction. This modified form of the streaming engine is used to generate a zero-parameter spectral Voice Activity Detection (VAD) coder which is scalable and uses the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) harmonic ratio stages which are responsible for the acoustic and arithmetical terminations that are actually detached from heavy machine learning constraints as practically all the acoustic feedback detached during the prediction phases at the encoder side is mitigated by a state-driven audio gating mechanism. Therefore, clearly the computation phase which is modified to delegate generative loads via WebSocket telemetry produces a bit stream which is highly scalable. This modified algorithm works well at both lower memory bounds and noisy environments. Quantitative evaluations were done by measuring the Time-To-First-Audio latency and RAM resource utilization across four hardware tiers in frontier regions and the results at various conditions were noted and compared with the previous standard architectures. © The Author(s).

title: Real-Time Voice-Based LLM Integration for XR Tutoring: A Prototype Implementation
venue: Proceedings - 2026 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and eXtended and Virtual Reality, AIxVR 2026
abstract: This paper presents a lightweight architecture for AI-driven tutoring in extended reality (XR) environments, integrating OpenAI's GPT-4o real-time API directly into Unitybased virtual reality (VR) to enable seamless voice-native interaction without external speech modules. Designed for taskbased learning, the tutor provides immediate, context-sensitive verbal feedback with adaptive brevity and low latency. A blockbased programming task demonstrates real-time evaluation, where user-assembled logic structures are analyzed and corrected through spoken responses. Across ten structured sessions and forty voice interactions, the prototype achieved consistent sub500 ms latency, generated under four minutes of total speech, and averaged 0.005 per turn. These results demonstrate the practical feasibility of low-overhead, real-time AI tutoring in XR and provide a foundation for future multimodal, context-aware learning environments. © 2026 IEEE.

title: REAL-TIME VR DIGITAL PRESENTATION OF ARCHITECTURAL HERITAGE BASED ON SCREEN FLUCTUATION OPTIMIZATION TECHNOLOGY
venue: Journal of Nonlinear and Convex Analysis
abstract: This study introduces a novel framework called HDL-MODTFO (Hybrid Deep Learning-based Multiple Object Detection and Tracking with Fluctuation Optimization), which is designed to enhance real-time virtual reality (VR) presentations of architectural heritage environments. Existing RGB-and LiDAR-based methods suffer from low accuracy, noise interference, and slow processing speed. To address these issues, HDL-MODTFO integrates solid-state Light Detection and Ranging (ss-LiDAR), pseudo-LiDAR, and Red-Green-Blue Depth (RGB-D) inputs through sensor fusion, ft also involves adaptive fuzzy filtering and contrast enhancement through Enhanced Moth Swarm Optimization (EMSO) for noise removal. The prcproccsscd data are combined and then segmented using a Lightweight Generative Adversarial Network (LGAN) with channel and position attention mechanisms to improve accuracy. For object detection and classification. VGG-f6 performs the extraction of features, while You Only Look Once (YOLOv4) performs classification. Finally, the Improved Un-scented Kalman Filter (IUKF) is applied for accurate object tracking and time-based mapping. The simulation of the model is performed under a comprehensive dataset consisting of LiDAR and stereo RGB images. The outcomes demonstrate the model's performance, achieving a notable accuracy of 98%, precision of 95%, a recall of 90%, an F-score of 93%, and a reduction in computation time of up to 30 seconds compared to existing methods. These results confirm the effectiveness of HDL-MODTFO in enhancing the real-time detection and tracking of architectural elements in digital heritage VR environments. © 2026 Yokohama Publications. To address these issues, HDL-MODTFO integrates solid-state Light Detection and Ranging (ss-LiDAR), pseudo-LiDAR, and Red-Green-Blue Depth (RGB-D) inputs through sensor fusion, ft also involves adaptive fuzzy filtering and contrast enhancement through Enhanced Moth Swarm Optimization (EMSO) for noise removal. The prcproccsscd data are combined and then segmented using a Lightweight Generative Adversarial Network (LGAN) with channel and position attention mechanisms to improve accuracy. For object detection and classification. VGG-f6 performs the extraction of features, while You Only Look Once (YOLOv4) performs classification. Finally, the Improved Un-scented Kalman Filter (IUKF) is applied for accurate object tracking and time-based mapping. The simulation of the model is performed under a comprehensive dataset consisting of LiDAR and stereo RGB images. The outcomes demonstrate the model's performance, achieving a notable accuracy of 98%, precision of 95%, a recall of 90%, an F-score of 93%, and a reduction in computation time of up to 30 seconds compared to existing methods. These results confirm the effectiveness of HDL-MODTFO in enhancing the real-time detection and tracking of architectural elements in digital heritage VR environments. © 2026 Yokohama Publications. title: Real-Time XR Maintenance Support Integrating Large Language Models in the Era of the Industrial Metaverse
venue: Applied Sciences (Switzerland)
abstract: Recent advancements in Artificial Intelligence and eXtended Reality (XR) have laid solid foundations for the development of a new paradigm in industrial maintenance under the light of Industry 5.0 framework. This research presents the design, development, and implementation of an XR-enabled remote maintenance framework that integrates real-time video collaboration, AI-assisted guidance, and a persistent digital asset knowledge layer based on Asset Administration Shells for Maintenance and Repair Operations (MRO). By combining fine-tuned Large Language Models (LLMs) with immersive XR interfaces, the proposed framework enables technicians to interact with virtual representations of industrial assets, access contextual instructions, and receive expert support remotely in real-time. Through seamless integration of historical MRO data, digital twins, and real-time sensor streams, the system facilitates dynamic fault diagnostics and Remaining Useful Life (RUL) estimation. Therefore, the proposed approach is positioned as a Metaverse-aligned implementation, combining synchronous multi-user collaboration, digital–physical coupling through digital twins, and semantic interoperability. The framework is validated through two industrial case studies, demonstrating its feasibility and practical impact on maintenance efficiency and knowledge transfer. The findings position the Industrial Metaverse as a transformative enabler in the future of AI-driven machinery health monitoring. © 2026 by the authors.

title: Reality as Imagined: Design and Evaluation of a TeleAbsence-Driven Extended Reality Experience for (Re) Interpreting Urban Cultural Heritage Narratives Across Time
venue: International Journal of Human-Computer Interaction
abstract: Visitors to Urban Cultural Heritage (UCH) often encounter official narratives but not the imaginations and relationships shaping its intangible aspects. Existing immersive experiences emphasize historical realities, overlooking personal and collective imaginations that shift with rapid development. To address this, we designed an Extended Reality (XR) experience around eight Hong Kong landmarks, enabling transitions between virtual and mixed-reality environments where users explore UCH narratives across past, present, and future. These narratives integrate (1) historical documentation with 360° visualizations and (2) images created in workshops supported by Generative AI tools. A mixed-method study with 24 participants examined their experiences and reflections. Results revealed deep immersion in both real and imagined worlds, as well as personal reinterpretations of UCH. This work demonstrates how XR can blend reality and imagination within one immersive experience and highlights design implications for archiving human imagination as an intangible form of cultural heritage. © 2025 Taylor & Francis Group, LLC.

title: RealityCraft: Automated Synthesis of Extended Reality Device Interaction Scripts from Natural Language Instructions
venue: Proceedings of the 2026 IEEE/ACM 48th International Conference on Software Engineering
abstract: Extended Reality (XR) apps have become increasingly popular across different domains, evidenced by its market growing to over $165 billion in 2024. Despite their widespread usage, XR apps present new challenges for automated software testing approaches, especially for testing script generation. XR apps have complicated action space from multi-device coordination with temporal precision. Besides, natural language instructions in XR apps usually have a large semantic gap with specific XR interactions. Therefore, previous testing script generation approaches on 2D apps such as Android can hardly be adopted into XR apps.To address these challenges, we introduce RealityScript, a domain-specific language designed to formalize spatially distributed, time-sensitive operations across heterogeneous XR devices. The language incorporates synchronized action blocks, device-agnostic input abstractions, and temporal operators to handle the complexities of XR interaction testing to describe spatial and temporal information. Building on RealityScript, we develop RealityCraft, a two-phase framework that translates natural language instructions into executable RealityScript scripts through semantic lifting and device binding. We conduct experiments on 125 XR interaction scenarios across three popular industrial-setting XR apps. Our evaluation shows that RealityCraft significantly outperforms state-of-the-art approaches in XR testing script generation accuracy (achieving nearly twice the BLEU score of the best baseline) and produces scripts with 74.07% replay success in runtime testing, compared to under 20% for existing approaches. This demonstrates the effectiveness of RealityCraft on the testing script generation of XR apps. We make all data public at https://sites.google.com/view/xr-testing-script-synthesis.

title: Reconstructing 360-Degree Memories in Virtual Reality with Generative Artificial Intelligence
venue: Proceedings - 2026 IEEE Conference on Virtual Reality and 3D User Interfaces Abstracts and Workshops, VRW 2026
abstract: Reminiscence is the activity of recalling and revisiting a memory. Past research highlights that reminiscence in older adults can promote healthy aging, improve psychological well-being, and could foster inter-generational communication. Virtual reality offers benefits to reminiscence as it allows users to reenact the past in embodied, immersive, and multi-sensory ways. A key challenge in VR reminiscence is the recreation of past scenes that are relevant and familiar to each user. Thus, this research seeks to evaluate and implement GenAI to prototype 360-degree scenes based on inputs that are relevant to each user. In particular, we examine the implementation 1) text-to-image and 2) panorama outpainting generation methods for 360-degree scenes. This study aims to bring personalization and control to the recreation of memories in VR. Moreover, this work strives to support the democratization of content creation in VR for users with various degrees of technical expertise. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Reconstructing the Design Workflow from Tradition to Algorithm in AI-Assisted Ceramic Product Design
venue: Proceedings of the 2nd International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Interaction Design
abstract: The increasing prevalence of artificial intelligence (AI) in design practice has sparked interest in AI-assisted creativity; however, existing research focuses on technical performance or visual effects, with little attention paid to how AI reshapes design processes in craft-based design fields. This study aims to fill this gap by exploring how AI-assisted tools transform the ceramic product design workflow from a process-oriented perspective. Using a qualitative, practice-based approach, this study reconstructs and compares traditional and AI-assisted ceramic product design workflows through design experiments and protocol analysis. The results show that AI primarily intervenes in the early ideation stage of the design process, introducing a generative layer, reorganizing iterative patterns, and front-loading the exploration process. Rather than replacing traditional practices, AI reshapes the workflow structure, shifting the designer's role from direct generation to curation, evaluation, and contextual judgment, while material experimentation, craft knowledge, and cultural understanding remain crucial in the later stages of the design process. This study contributes to design research by providing empirical evidence from a craft-based design field and proposing a workflow reconstruction method to facilitate human-AI collaboration. By positioning AI as a workflow intermediary embedded within design practice, this study offers a deeper understanding of how AI supports innovation in ceramic product design while maintaining cultural continuity and craft integrity.

title: Reconstruction of University Art Education in the Era of Artificial Intelligence and Mixed Reality: A Curriculum Design Framework Based on the ASSURE Model
venue: International Journal of Special Education
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) and mixed reality (MR) technologies are driving the transformation of university art education from traditional skills training and work appreciation to digital creation, immersive experience, and cross-media expression. However, current applications mostly remain at the tool level, lacking a systematic and transferable teaching design framework. Based on the ASSURE instructional design model, this paper integrates the concept of "borderless learning" and extends the LeSMaT (Borderless) framework to the field of art education, proposing "Learning Science and Arts Together in a Borderless World" (LeSAT (Borderless)), and constructs an AI-MR enhanced university art course framework. This framework unfolds around six stages: learner analysis, goal setting, medium selection, teaching implementation, learning participation, and evaluation. Taking university art courses as an example, a four-stage progressive teaching process is designed: interest stimulation, skill training, immediate feedback, and digital creation, and a five-dimensional course goal is constructed, covering physical skills, artistic creation, digital literacy, individual empowerment, and social collaboration. From the perspective of educational psychology, this framework helps to reduce technology anxiety, enhance self-efficacy, increase learning persistence, and promote the development of higher-order thinking. As a conceptual study, this paper provides a structured and transferable theoretical path for the reconstruction of university art courses driven by technology. In addition, the flexibility of this framework makes it potentially applicable to special education settings, where learner-centered design and multimodal technology integration can address diverse sensory, motor, and cognitive needs. © 2026 Authors.

title: Reflective Human–AI Collaboration: Preparing STEM Students for Future Work with XR Labs and LLM Technologies
venue: Learning and Analytics in Intelligent Systems
abstract: Cross-reality laboratories such as digital twins are now increasingly making their way into university laboratory learning at all levels of study in STEM subjects. In addition to subject-related skills development, students can also generate skills for collaborative, agile learning 4.0. The collaborative project KICK 4.0 picks up on these lines of development, but links them with completely new types of AI skills requirements that are becoming increasingly necessary with the growing spread of AI-based natural language processing systems in an evolving workplace. By actively engaging students, teachers and other stakeholders in reflecting upon both the potential and limitations of human–AI collaboration, this project contributes significantly to preparing future professionals for dynamic occupational contexts. This chapter provides an overview of current research, assesses contemporary AI tools and their applicability in educational settings, and critically examines experiences arising from human–AI interactions in the XR-based instructional laboratory. Ultimately, by defining a first draft of pedagogical requirements, KICK 4.0 underscores the importance of thoughtful integration of emerging technologies into education in general and laboratory instruction in particular to sustainably enhance human skillsets and maintain meaningful human engagement in collaborative work environments. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.

title: Reframe: Collaborative AI Scene Editing in 360° Multiplayer VR
venue: Proceedings - SIGGRAPH 2026 Immersive Pavilion
abstract: Reframe is a multiplayer virtual reality experience where groups collectively edit 360° photographic environments using generative AI. Participants inhabit an immersive 360° or panoramic image and point at areas they wish to modify. They then speak together about what they want to see, and the system transcribes and summarizes their dialogue into a prompt. AI imagery is subsequently composited into the selected area. Building on prior research documenting how collaborative storytelling emerges through voice-based interaction with panoramic imagery, Reframe translates these affordances into a portable VR installation. The result invites participants to treat the panorama as an archive for remembering or a canvas for exploration.Supplementary Video: https://youtu.be/oBRH6CAxUgk

title: Refugio: a voice-driven generative virtual reality “safe place” for personalized emotion regulation – feasibility and usability study
venue: Frontiers in Virtual Reality
abstract: Introduction: Virtual Reality (VR) has emerged as a pivotal tool for mental health interventions, paving the way for innovative approaches to emotional regulation. While the customization of therapeutic “safe places” is believed to enhance outcomes, existing applications often depend on inflexible, pre-configured content. This paper introduces Refugio, a groundbreaking VR application designed to bridge this gap through an integrated, real-time personalization pipeline powered by a self-hosted Large Language Model (LLM) and an efficient voice-to-3D generative pipeline. Methods: We conducted a feasibility and usability study with 30 non-clinical participants to evaluate the feasibility and user acceptance of this natural language-driven approach, while preliminarily exploring its potential to support emotional outcomes and immersion while minimizing cognitive workload. We assessed usability (using the System Usability Scale - SUS), cognitive load (NASA-TLX), immersion (RJPQ), and emotional state before and after (Self-Assessment Manikin - SAM). Results: The study provided compelling preliminary evidence of the system’s feasibility and high user acceptance. Refugio achieved an “Excellent” mean SUS score of 86.33, alongside low reported mental demand and frustration. Participants showed strong engagement, creating 147 objects, and reported positive emotional shifts, with the majority experiencing increased valence (21 out of 30) and decreased arousal (19 out of 30). Discussion: This study demonstrates that Refugio’s architecture is a viable and well-received method for implementing deep generative personalization. Our findings suggest that this natural language driven approach adeptly balances creative freedom with high usability and low cognitive load, thereby establishing a robust foundation for future clinical validation. title: ReHome Earth: A VR-Based Concept Validation for AI-Driven Space Homesickness Interventions
venue: TEI 2026 - Proceedings of 20th International Conference on Tangible, Embedded, and Embodied Interaction
abstract: Space exploration has advanced rapidly, but the emotional needs of astronauts on long-duration missions remain underexplored. We present ReHome Earth, a dual-component design approach addressing space homesickness: 1) a future-oriented installation concept integrating transparent OLED displays with spaceship windows for real-time Earth connectivity, and 2) a functional VR prototype simulating astronaut isolation for testing AI-generated content effectiveness. Since accessing astronauts during missions is impossible, we conducted concept validation with terrestrial participants experiencing geographic displacement. Through evaluation with 84 proxy participants and 6 HCI experts, we demonstrate strong emotional resonance and validate three design implications: emotional pacing mechanisms, explainable biophysical feedback systems, and evolution from individual tools to collective affective infrastructure. Our contributions include a technically feasible space installation concept, a functional VR prototype for space HCI research, and empirical insights into the design of AI-driven emotional support systems for extreme isolation environments. © 2026 Copyright held by the owner/author(s)

title: Reliability of Edge AI in XR-Based Health Data Capture: An Experimental Study on GPU Offloading and Semantic Stability
venue: IEEE Access
abstract: Edge artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly required in extended reality (XR) healthcare systems to characterize latency behavior under controlled execution constraints, energy efficiency, and privacy-preserving processing of sensitive patient data. This paper presents an edge-native multimodal XR architecture for structured health data capture, integrating automatic speech recognition, quantized large language model inference, and deterministic adaptation within a fully on-device pipeline. We conduct a controlled experimental evaluation of heterogeneous graphics processing unit (GPU) offloading levels (GPU Layers = 0, 20, 30), with n = 30 runs per configuration, and quantify latency-energy scaling under distinct embedded power modes (7 W and 15 W). Beyond conventional performance metrics, we introduce semantic stability indicators for structured JSON-based clinical extraction, including schema validity, completion rate, and critical-field null rate. Results reveal a systematic latency-semantic trade-off: aggressive GPU offloading reduces end-to-end latency but may induce complete loss of critical structured fields under specific configurations, reaching a 100% null rate in extreme cases. The findings on the evaluated platform demonstrate that edge optimization strategies in XR healthcare pipelines should be assessed not only in terms of computational efficiency but also in terms of semantic reliability. The proposed architecture and evaluation framework provide experimentally reproducible characterization for designing trustworthy edge AI systems in real-time clinical XR environments. © 2026 The Authors.

title: Remember Me, Not Save Me: A Collective Memory System for Evolving Virtual Identities in Augmented Reality
venue: VRCAI 2025 - 20th International Conference on Virtual Reality Continuum and its Applications in Industry
abstract: This paper presents "Remember Me, Not Save Me,"an AR & AI system enabling virtual citizens to develop personality through collective dialogue. Core innovations include: Dynamic Collective Memory (DCM) model with narrative tension mechanisms for handling contradictory memories; State-Reflective Avatar for ambient explainability; and Geo-Cultural Context Anchoring for local identity. Deployed at the 2024 Jinan Biennale, the system demonstrated stable personality emergence (ISTP type via Apply Magic Sauce analysis) from over 2,500 public interactions. We provide a framework for designing evolving digital entities that transform collective memory into coherent identity. © 2025 Copyright held by the owner/author(s).

title: Research and Development of a Youth Psychological Counseling System Based on Large Models and Anime Representation
venue: Proceedings of the 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Interaction Design
abstract: This work creates and implements an AI-powered psychological therapy system for adolescents, focused on a virtual persona dubbed “Teacher Xiaohua.” Through guided talks, the system assists teenagers in expressing their inner thoughts, identifying issues linked to learning, emotions, stress, and family communication, and creating mental health assessment reports to provide scientific counsel and therapies for psychological well-being. The system combines advanced AI technologies and finely crafted interface methods. A guided conversational framework and a multi-level subject change system provide natural and fluid talks. The employment of an anime-style virtual character increases engagement and accessibility. The system uses large language models (LLMs) to create responses, includes historical data for contextual memory, and provides an emotionally engaged experience via the virtual character. The virtual character's expressions and movements are managed by the VTube Studio platform, which is often used in VTuber scenarios. Pre-designed expression templates, audio-driven synchronization, and the random insertion of dynamic effects enable realistic interactions. Furthermore, the system conducts detailed evaluations of users’ mental states by extracting keywords and quantifying evaluation criteria, resulting in individualized recommendations. Testing shows that the system has tremendous potential in mental health assessment, providing a friendly and efficient mental health support tool for adolescents while also paving a new research path for technological innovation in the field of psychological counseling.

title: Research on AI Agent Task Flow Modeling and Intelligent Review System for Contract Review
venue: Proceedings of the 2nd International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Interaction Design
abstract: In the global business landscape, contract review has long relied on manual processes, leading to issues such as low efficiency, high costs, and heightened legal and financial risks. Existing AI-assisted approaches—whether rule-based templates, statistical machine learning, or end-to-end LLMs—suffer from limitations such as poor generalization, dependence on annotated data, or uncontrollable outputs, and they fail to deconstruct the cognitive process of review in a refined manner. This paper introduces an AI Agent framework to model contract review as a multi-agent task flow and develops an intelligent review system. The process is decomposed into subtasks within an architecture comprising a Management and Coordination Agent Hub, Specialized Execution Agents, and a Knowledge Support Layer. Additionally, the study develops an information extraction algorithm based on LLMs and structured prompts, as well as a hybrid risk identification algorithm combining rules and semantic models. The revision further clarifies cost-aware selective invocation, confidence-based conflict resolution, separate precision-recall evaluation, and a human-in-the-loop knowledge update workflow.

title: Research on AI-Empowered Visual Translation and Innovative Communication of Bashu Regional Cultural Heritage
venue: Proceedings of the 2nd International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Interaction Design
abstract: With the advancement of generative AI technology, its applications in visual design have garnered significant attention. To address challenges in traditional regional cultural visual communication—including limited design efficiency, insufficient creative expression, and difficulties in translating cultural symbols—this study focuses on Bashu regional culture and establishes a cultural visual design research framework based on AIGC (ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE GENERATED CONTENT). The research first systematically collects visual resources of Bashu culture, creating a cultural visual database that includes traditional patterns, cultural symbols, performing arts, and architectural elements. Subsequently, through cultural feature extraction and PROMPT prompt design, generative AI models generate cultural visual images, which are then integrated via a collaborative “AI generation + designer optimization” model. During the experimental phase, the AI model generated 120 visual design proposals across three categories: cultural posters, product packaging, and cultural illustrations. Thirty design professionals were invited to evaluate the proposals, and a five-point Likert scale was used to construct a cultural visual communication evaluation system. Results showed that all metrics averaged over 4.0, with the visual creativity index reaching 4.47, indicating strong performance in creative expression and cultural symbol presentation. Compared to traditional design processes, AI-assisted design improved creativity scores by approximately 16% and significantly enhanced design efficiency. The research findings demonstrate that AIGC technology can effectively expand the creative space for cultural visual design, while providing innovative design methodologies and practical approaches for regional cultural visual communication.

title: Research on AIGC-3D Printing Collaborative Design Method for Personalized Wearable Devices
venue: Proceedings of the 2nd International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Interaction Design, AIVRID 2026
abstract: Aiming at the problems of disconnection among creative generation, physiological adaptation and additive manufacturing, insufficient manufacturability constraints and low design automation in personalized wearable device design, this paper proposes a closed-loop collaborative design framework embedded with manufacturing constraints. The framework adopts a three-tier modular architecture: design semantic-to-visual mapping, physiological data-driven geometric constraint solving, and additive manufacturing-oriented performance optimization. By integrating 3D printing process priors into the generative stage and multi-objective topology optimization, the framework realizes end-to-end intelligent customization from text to printable models. Verified on a VR headset mask, the design cycle is shortened from days to minutes; the average fitting accuracy reaches 0.37 mm; the average printing yield reaches 98.5%; and the model weight is reduced by 25.2%. The method provides a reusable paradigm for the large-scale personalized production of wearable devices. © 2026 Copyright held by the owner/author(s).

title: Research on AIGC-based Visual Translation and Multimodal Interaction Design for Cultural Heritage
venue: Proceedings of the 2nd International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Interaction Design
abstract: This paper proposes and validates a lightweight framework aimed at utilizing Generative Artificial Intelligence (AIGC) to address the issues of homogenized visual styles and superficial interactive experiences in the digital display of cultural heritage. The core of the framework consists of a visual feature deconstruction model based on painting expertise, a low-threshold stylized translation workflow based on Stable Diffusion and LoRA, and a multimodal interaction prototype system integrated with AIGC real-time generation capability. Using Han Dynasty stone reliefs as an empirical case, this study collects quantitative and qualitative data through a controlled experiment (N=60). The results show that the visual content generated by this method significantly outperforms traditional 3D modeling methods in cultural recognizability (improvement of 42.3%, p<0.01); the developed interaction system also performs better in user experience metrics such as immersion, cultural understanding, and engagement intention. This study provides a feasible low-technical-threshold pathway for researchers with art backgrounds to participate in digital cultural heritage creation. The related process has been successfully applied in digital art course teaching.

title: Research on Creative Design and Immersive Experience Optimization of Cultural and Tourism Scenes Based on Virtual Reality
venue: Proceedings of 2025 International Conference on Digital Society and Intelligent Computing, ICDSIC 2025
abstract: Virtual reality (VR) technology, as a revolutionary medium for the digital dissemination and experience of cultural heritage (CH), has shown great potential in enhancing cultural accessibility, public participation, and promoting sustainable tourism. However, the current mainstream VR tourism applications are generally limited by pre-set static content, fixed linear narratives, and limited interactivity, resulting in stagnant content updates and shallow interactive experiences, making it difficult to stimulate deep emotional resonance and lasting "presence"among users. To overcome the experience bottleneck of "one size fits all", this paper proposes an Adaptive Cultural Tourism Scene Framework based on Affective Computing and Generative Networks (ACF-GAN), which is based on emotion computing and generative adversarial networks. This framework constructs a "perception generation"closed-loop system, with the core mechanism being: firstly, by integrating multimodal physiological sensors, real-time collection and decoding of users' emotional and cognitive states are quantified into a dynamic "immersion index"; Secondly, this index serves as a condition to drive a deep generative adversarial network to reconstruct cultural and tourism scenes in real-time, dynamically, and creatively. This kind of refactoring is not a complete replacement, but rather acts on the basic scene model in the form of "scene increments". To verify the effectiveness of the framework, this paper conducted quantitative and qualitative experiments on the "OpenHeritage BioSignal"dataset. The results indicate that ACF-GAN demonstrates significant superiority over static VR and non adaptive generative models in terms of subjective immersion and user engagement metrics, while ensuring acceptable computational overhead. This study confirms the effectiveness of the closed-loop framework in achieving personalized and deeply immersive cultural and tourism experiences, providing new theoretical and technological paths for the intelligent and creative design of VR cultural and tourism in the future. © 2025 Copyright held by the owner/author(s).

title: Research on design of interactive entertainment system for second language acquisition based on Speech-Gesture multimodal perception
venue: Entertainment Computing
abstract: Traditional second language acquisition tools have a single interaction, a lack of immersion and self-adaptation ability, and are difficult to stimulate learning motivation. This study designs and implements a second language acquisition interactive entertainment system integrating voice-gesture multimodal perception, integrating an Extended Reality (XR) immersive environment, and an intelligent interaction mechanism. The system architecture includes voice emotion recognition, gesture motion capture, and a multi-modal feature cascade fusion algorithm, and adopts generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) to dynamically adjust the feedback and narrative direction of virtual characters to realize content adaptation based on user emotional state. In order to verify the effectiveness of the system, 30 s-language learners were recruited to carry out a comparative experiment: the experimental group used this system to complete interactive tasks in XR scenes, while the control group used a traditional APP to learn. Assessment indicators include multimodal recognition accuracy, learning effect (vocabulary test), user experience (immersion questionnaire), and emotional adaptability. The results show that the recognition rate of multi-modal fusion reaches 94.3%, which is 12.7% higher than that of single modal fusion; The average post-test score of vocabulary in the experimental group was 85.6 (72.4 in the control group, p < 0.01); The user experience immersion score is 4.6/5; The matching accuracy of emotional feedback and user status was 91.2%. The innovations of this study are as follows: 1) Proposing a speech-gesture collaborative perception framework to enhance interaction robustness through spatiotemporal alignment; 2) Building an emotion-driven adaptive feedback mechanism to dynamically optimize learning content and role behavior; 3) Designing XR immersive second language acquisition scenarios, integrating generative narrative and multi-modal interaction, and enhancing learning motivation and entertainment experience. This study provides empirical evidence supporting the effectiveness of multimodal intelligent interaction in enhancing learning performance and user experience within XR-based environments. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. title: Research on Digital Visual Communication and Style Adaptation Based on Generative AI
venue: Proceedings of the 2nd International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Interaction Design
abstract: Traditional visual communication design has problems with long creation cycles and difficult style control, making it difficult to ssmeet the multi platform and high-frequency content production needs in digital communication scenarios. In response to the above challenges, we propose a style adaptive generative AI for digital visual communication called StyleGrad. This method uses MT5 as the basic model for extending prompt words, modeling style intensity as a gradient distribution in the semantic space, achieving automatic extension from short style words to multi-level detailed prompt words. We design Style Intensity Contrastive Loss (SIC Loss) to form an ordered semantic distribution of different intensity descriptions through triplet constraints, and introduce cross modal consistency loss constraints to generate semantic alignment between text and style images, ensuring that the expanded prompts faithfully preserve the core visual semantics of the target style. In addition, we constructed a style description dataset containing 50 visual styles across four categories and 5000 samples, each with standardized low, medium, and high intensity descriptions paired with reference images. The experimental results showed that StyleGrad achieved a generation quality of FID 23.76 and CLIP Score 0.318, with a style intensity control accuracy of 76.42%. Compared to the suboptimal method, it improved by 8.01%, 3.25%, and 3. 14% respectively, validating the effectiveness of the proposed approach in controllable style generation for digital visual communication.

title: Research on image enhancement of smart home product layout scene based on virtual reality
venue: International Journal of Computer Applications in Technology
abstract: To elevate the quality of image enhancement for smart home product layout scenes and expedite processing times, a study focused on virtual reality-based enhancement of these scenes has been undertaken. Initially, a virtual reality framework is employed to create an indoor environment for smart homes, with the ISGSA algorithm model utilised to generate this environment. Subsequently, the attributes of each constituent element are amalgamated and fed into a generator to produce a novel indoor scene. Ultimately, a conditional generative adversarial network is devised to formulate a composite loss function, integrating channel colour loss, structural feature loss and smoothness loss. This loss function is instrumental in achieving image enhancement. Experimental findings reveal that the proposed method attains an average information entropy of 8.846, with an image enhancement processing duration of merely 3.9 s. © The Author(s) 2026. title: Research on Immersive Cultural Heritage Exhibition Integrating XR and Digital Narrative
venue: Proceedings of the 2026 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Generative Design
abstract: With the growing demand for digital preservation and dissemination of cultural heritage, traditional exhibition methods have increasingly revealed limitations in terms of immersion, interactivity, and narrative depth. To enhance the effectiveness of cultural heritage communication, this study investigates immersive exhibition approaches that integrate extended reality (XR) with digital storytelling, establishing a multi-tiered immersive display system tailored for cultural heritage contexts. The system utilizes cultural heritage data to digitally reconstruct historical scenes through 3D reconstruction technology, combined with XR rendering engines to create immersive spatial environments. It incorporates digital storytelling mechanisms-including timeline narratives, character-driven narratives, and scenario-based storytelling-to dynamically present cultural content, while employing multimodal interaction technologies to enhance user engagement. Furthermore, the study develops a user experience evaluation model encompassing immersion, interactivity, emotional resonance, and cultural comprehension, analyzing system performance through multidimensional metrics. Results demonstrate that this methodology significantly improves user immersion experiences and cultural understanding, strengthening emotional connections and memory retention in cultural communication. This work establishes a novel paradigm integrating spatial computing with narrative design for digital cultural heritage exhibitions, providing theoretical and methodological support for the development of smart museums and digital cultural tourism.

title: Research on Innovation of AIGC-Integrated Digital Media Art Creation and Communication Modes
venue: Proceedings of 2025 2nd International Conference on Digital Economy and Computer Science, DECS 2025
abstract: With the rapid development of Artificial Intelligence Generated Content (AIGC) technology, the field of digital media art has ushered in unprecedented opportunities for innovation. This study focuses on exploring the integration of AIGC into digital media art creation and the corresponding innovations in communication modes. First, it analyzes the current status of digital media art creation and communication, identifying the limitations of traditional models in terms of efficiency, personalization, and audience interaction. Then, a novel AIGC-integrated digital media art creation framework is proposed, which combines generative adversarial networks (GANs), diffusion models, and transformer-based language models to enhance the diversity and creativity of artworks. For the communication mode, a multi-channel interactive communication model is designed, leveraging social media platforms, virtual reality (VR) exhibition halls, and blockchain-based digital asset management systems to improve the reach and influence of digital media art.To verify the effectiveness of the proposed framework and model, experiments are conducted from two aspects: creation efficiency and communication effect. In the creation efficiency experiment, 50 professional digital media artists and 50 non-professional participants are invited to create artworks using the traditional method and the AIGC-integrated method respectively. The results show that the AIGC-integrated method reduces the creation time by an average of 62.3% and improves the diversity of artworks by 45.8% compared with the traditional method. In the communication effect experiment, two groups of artworks (one created with the AIGC-integrated method and the other with the traditional method) are promoted through different communication channels. The data indicate that the multi-channel interactive communication model increases the audience engagement rate by 78.5% and the artwork sharing rate by 63.2% compared with the single-channel communication model. © 2025 Copyright held by the owner/author(s).

title: Research on Liaoning Intangible Cultural Heritage Identification and Digital Teaching System Based on Computer Vision and Generative AI Technologies
venue: Proceedings of the 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Interaction Design
abstract: Although there is no distinctive header, this is the abstract. This paper addresses the challenges of low recognition accuracy and weak teaching interaction in the digital preservation of Liaoning's intangible cultural heritage by integrating computer vision and generative AI. This study constructs a parallel architecture combining a multi-scale attention CNN and a domain-adapted Transformer, achieving dynamic alignment of visual and semantic features through mutual information guidance. A sample generation module based on an improved WGAN is designed to triple the sample size of scarce intangible cultural heritage artifacts, such as Fuzhou shadow puppetry. Finally, a three-tiered “cloud-edge-end” digital teaching system is developed, integrating resource libraries, recognition and display, personalized recommendations, and virtual interaction modules. Experiments based on the self-built LNMD-2024 dataset (26,800 samples) demonstrated that the model achieved 92.3% recognition accuracy and 92.1% F1 score, representing improvements of 8.5%-9.2% over traditional methods. The generated sample structure similarity reached 0.89. The system response latency was ≤480ms under 500 concurrent users, and GPU utilization remained stable at 75%. This research provides a technical paradigm for the intelligent inheritance of intangible cultural heritage and has increased user retention by 42%.

title: Research on Optimizing AI-Assisted Film and Television VFX Production
venue: Proceedings of the 2nd International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Interaction Design
abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) has opened up new possibilities for efficiency innovation in film and television visual effects (VFX) production. The traditional VFX production process involves creative design via hand-drawing or Photoshop in the early stage, followed by 3D modeling based on the design drafts, and finally rendering. This process is often time-consuming and inefficient. This paper proposes a VFX production method that integrates AI with the traditional workflow, namely “Doubao AI for rendering generation → Tripo AI for preliminary modeling → Maya for model refinement and animation production → Unreal Engine for rendering”. The feasibility and advantages of this model are verified through comparative experiments. The experimental results show that the most prominent role of AI in film and television VFX production lies in early-stage creative divergence and auxiliary modeling. It can effectively improve production efficiency while ensuring work quality, providing an efficient production mode for the film and television post-production workflow.
